Introduction

You may wonder, as do I, and as do people

everywhere: how could this great scholar have gained

access to such truth, when all of the earlier scholars

and the great guides and imams failed to do so? I

would reply to you: a person has nothing except

what they strive for.

Indeed, people are differentiated through their actions.

This is true even for the Envoys (Messengers) and

noble Prophets… and there will be a different level for

everyone according to their deeds in this world.

Our own great scholar Mohammad Emin Sheikho

was given awareness and understanding by Al’lah,

and he was distinguished by his outstanding deeds

and his great and humane sacrifices. Al’lah did not

give him anything except that which he deserved.

God says, “And We sent it down deservedly, and

with righteousness it came down.” ﴿1﴾

1 e Holy Qur’an, Fortress (Surah) 17, e Night Journey (al-Isra’), verse 105.

— صفحة 12 — ﴿11﴾

The True Benefits of Almsgiving

timely plan of the Wise Arranger brought this story to

mind long after it had been forgotten by most people.

We were most fortunate to hear the details from the

man who was central to this story. And as we learnt a great

lesson and understood the high purpose behind it, we wanted

to relate it to our dear readers so that they too might learn from

it and be relieved from the hardship they face in this life.

Master Salah al-Din Sheikho, a son of the eminent

scholar, Mohammad Emin Sheikho, recalled this story when

he was afflicted with an apparently incurable disease and

spent four long days suffering excruciating pain. During this

time he remembered the recommendation of God’s Envoy

(cpth)

1 which states, “Help your patients to be cured by

almsgiving”, and how his father had educated him to resort

to this solution whenever troubles assailed him.

Salah had personal experience of the great effect and

benefits of almsgiving whenever he offered it, so there and

then, he gave a considerable amount of alms to poor and

needy families and thus he was healed of his illness and

restored to good health.

1 (cpth) is an acronym for ‘communication with Al’lah and peace are through him.’

— صفحة 13 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿12﴾

His recent recovery was still fresh in the mind of Master

Salah when we, a few days later and by God’s Arrangement,

met with him. He was happy and expressed his gratitude for

the high education his father had given him in this respect

and the refinement he had received by his instruction on

adopting the methods of God’s Envoy (cpth) in treatment

and in all other fields.

This difficult situation had allowed him to bring to mind

a story from his past when he was still a child and how, by

almsgiving, his father saved him from suffering permanent

deformity of his hand.

As Salah began to recite his story, we saw his eyes alight

with gratitude to God, the High Benefactor, and full of joy

at its memory.

Two young boys were playing together happily in the

courtyard of their large Arabian-style house, following one

another and filling the house with innocent laughter. Salah,

the younger boy, liked to sit on the shoulders of his elder

brother Fathi; so Fathi helped him to climb up, then he held

his hands and began walking around and turning right and

left in order to frighten his little brother, but which only

served to increase the child’s pleasure and laughter. In this

light-hearted, playful manner the little boy was sometimes

carried on his brother’s shoulders, and other times he jumped

down and ran off to be chased by Fathi; these were always

enjoyable happy moments for both boys.

This is how it was when, suddenly, a sad event interrupted

their play and wiped out their pleasure. This happened when

— صفحة 14 —

The True Benefits of Almsgiving ﴿13﴾

Salah was riding on his brother’s shoulders and within an

instant he lost his balance and fell to the ground. The little

boy fell without warning, so Fathi was unable to grab him to

break his fall.

The little boy cried out sharply in pain… but Mohammad

Emin, the boys’ father had heard the cry, and soon came from

his room to see what the matter was. He saw his son lying on

the floor crying, so he rushed towards him and asked what

had happened and where, exactly, he was hurt.

‘Oh… Daddy,’ the boy answered, moaning, ‘it’s my

hand… it hurts… I fell on it.’

The merciful father examined the area of pain on his

son’s hand and found swelling and discolouration of the

skin at the forearm, near to the elbow. It seemed that the

fall had resulted in a hairline fracture or a break in the arm.

Without delay, the noble master put on his outdoor

clothes and took his son to a physician to examine his hand.

Indeed, when the physician finished the examination, he

confirmed the father’s guess that the arm was broken and

decided that it should be splinted. This was attended to in

the proper way and he told the noble master to visit him

again with his son after two months, the length of time

needed for the break to mend.

The little boy could hardly wait for the time to pass and

the day that he would be able to use his hand normally once

again. But when his father took him back to the physician to

remove the splint, he was shocked to see that the child was

unable to extend his hand normally. Worse still, it had

developed an alarming tremor.

— صفحة 15 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿14﴾

The situation, as viewed, could not be considered as normal

articular calcination that would need a short time to correct

itself and then the joint would function naturally once again.

The case certainly seemed to be more serious than that.

The doctor carefully examined the boy’s hand and found

that the tendons had atrophied, causing the hand to become

fixed, and that he would not be able to use it any more.

Faced with this distressing situation, the noble master

wasted no time and took his beloved son by the hand and

headed off in search of the surgeon-general of Syria, Dr. Nazmi

al-Qabbani. The doctor was also the head of the National

Hospital

2 in Damascus, and this is where the worried father

went seeking advice for the treatment of his beloved son.

Because of their old friendship which stretched back to

childhood days when they lived in the same quarter, the

head of the hospital welcomed his guest warmly and was

extremely interested in the critical case of his friend’s little

son. He immediately sent for all the neurologists working in

the hospital for them to examine the boy’s damaged hand

and to advise him of their joint diagnosis.

But, unfortunately, they were unable to add anything to

the diagnosis of the first doctor who was consulted.

They said to their director that the nerves in the child’s

hand had shortened through lack of use while it was held

immobile in a splint and they thought that, in their opinion,

the case was incurable.

2 The National Hospital was the only hospital in Syria at that time.

— صفحة 16 —

The True Benefits of Almsgiving ﴿15﴾

However, Dr al-Qabbani was not prepared to let the

mater rest there. He picked up the telephone and made the

first of many calls to famous hospitals all over the world.

He had decided to send the boy by the first plane leaving

Damascus to whichever hospital might provide an effective

treatment for the boy’s case.

He phoned to the American Hospital in Lebanon which

was equal in levels of technology and experience to the

hospitals of America. He also phoned many hospitals in

Turkey, Europe and other countries. But these hospitals also

gave him the same negative response he had received from

the doctors in the National Hospital. They were all agreed

that the case looked hopeless and there was not even the

slightest possibility that the child’s hand could make any

improvement. Thus, this physical disability would remain

with the boy for the rest of his life.

The crushing news came as a disaster to the ears of the

loving father, as his thoughts travelled to the wretched future

that awaited his beloved son; so he asked his friend Dr.

Nazmi in a sad voice, ‘Are you sure of what you say, doctor?

Will my son’s condition stay like this for the rest of his life?’

Being affected by the heart breaking situation of the

merciful father, the doctor replied, ‘I’m sorry, Bey! But it is a

fact, and I am sure of what I say. I have telephoned medical

experts in many hospitals around the world and, as you have

heard, they have all agreed that this case is incurable. I am

really sorry, but we can do nothing for your son.’

— صفحة 17 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿16﴾

On hearing this affirmation from the head doctor, the

noble master felt as if the world had grown dark before his

eyes and a heavy weight had settled on his chest. An

overwhelming feeling of great sorrow and discomfort had

pervaded his heart when he looked at his son and thought

about his future. He imagined him as a young man, standing

handicapped among his healthy friends. Every time he

looked at the child this distressing picture returned to his

mind causing his grief and pain to increase even further,

creating such pain in his heart because he felt unable to help

his child and relieve him of this severe difficulty.

Silence reigned in the doctor’s office as he shared his

friend’s sorrow and grief. Alas, modern medicine had only

offered disappointment to both the father and his son!

Without uttering another word, the tender-hearted father

stretched his hand towards his son’s healthy hand and they

left the room calmly, hand in hand.

All during the way home, the father remained silent, but

his deep sadness was clearly etched on his face. When they

eventually reached the house they found the mother

impatiently waiting for their return. She was shocked by the

sight of her little son, but she hid her feelings from the child

and followed her husband to his own room so as to ask him

about the matter. When the husband saw his wife coming he

quickly concealed the signs of sadness that the heart-rending

news had imposed on his face.

‘Oh, Abu Fathi…’ she said to her husband, ‘what did the

doctor say about Salah’s hand? I hope you have brought me

— صفحة 18 —

The True Benefits of Almsgiving ﴿17﴾

good news’… and she stood silently, but on tenterhooks,

looking at the eyes of her husband as she waited for the

answer.

To avoid her suffering what he was suffering, the noble

master preferred to keep the true condition of their son’s

hand to himself for a while, therefore he replied, ‘No, no…

Um Fathi, do not worry. The case is simple; it only needs

two or maybe three months to be healed and return to its

normal condition.’

The compassionate mother could hardly curb her tears,

and she said in a choking voice, ‘Oh, thank God… Praise be

to God that it needs only two or three months to be cured,

and not more.’ By his merciful conduct, Mohammad Emin

made his wife believe that the case was not serious and so he

relieved her of her anxiety and spared her the terrible feelings

of extreme grief that she had not suffered so far.

Mohammad Emin’s wife then resumed her daily chores

in the house leaving the noble master standing and looking

around him in confusion.

A series of questions struck his mind that ignited even

further flames of grief and pain in his heart, ‘What can I do

about this terrible situation? Is there nothing I might resort

to in order to save my son from living this permanent,

difficult situation? Can’t I help him? Will he have to live

with this deformity for the rest of his life?’

Faced with the reality of this bitter fact, the merciful father

was consumed by sorrow for his son, and the earth, for all its

vastness, seemed to close in upon him. So, he grabbed a chair

— صفحة 19 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿18﴾

and, opening the door of his room, he rushed out to the street

where he banged the chair down beside the main door and

plopped on to the seat.

It was acustom of the men of Damascus at that time to

sit on wooden chairs in front of their houses during the

afternoon hours, where they would usually read the Holy

Qur’an. The women, however, did not normally leave their

homes except when it was strictly necessary.

Our compassionate man was sitting there with all his

thoughts concentrated on the difficult condition of his son.

He was focusing on finding a solution when suddenly he

remembered a noble saying of God’s Envoy (cpth) which

states, “Help your patients to be cured by almsgiving.”

He stood up as if a new life had gushed inside him to

dispel the distress he was suffering; then he dashed into his

house heading for a particular place in his room from where

he drew out a bundle containing fourteen golden liras. This

was all the money he had at that time.

He was fully aware of the momentous experience he had

just had, so he rushed out of the house, heading for al-

Akrad Mountain where many destitute families suffering

dire need and poverty were living.

He set about visiting these families, one by one, after he had

decided to give each family two golden liras: a sum that was

enough to support them fully for a considerable period of time,

two months at least. He spent a long time in accomplishing his

noble aim and it was late when he returned home, having

distributed all the golden liras he had.

— صفحة 20 —

The True Benefits of Almsgiving ﴿19﴾

Even though he was exhausted, his face was glowing and

appeared to shine with an inner radiance. He felt his suffering

becoming less; however, he still felt the weight of Salah’s

impediment impressed deeply on his mind, and his heart

burn with grief whenever he thought about him.

He had taken every possible step and sacrificed all the

money he had in order to save his son, and then he committed

his cause to God, the Controller of everything.

His family was all asleep when he returned home, so he went

to his own room and closed the door. There, he undressed, put

on his pyjamas and lay in his bed, and it was only a few minutes

before he surrendered his exhausted body to sleep.

That evening, silence prevailed throughout the house

because all the members of the family were touched by the sad

affliction of little Salah. And the merciful father was more

deeply affected than all the others for he was the only one to

be fully aware of the magnitude of the misfortune, and its

probable outcome on the course of his son’s life.

It was dawn when the venerable master woke up and

came out of his room to make the ritual ablution for prayer.

As he passed through the courtyard he saw Salah swinging

on the seesaw with his damaged hand. He stopped and gazed

at him in wonder. To be sure of what he had seen, he called

out to his son, ‘Salah, bring me a glass of water, son.’

‘With pleasure, Daddy.’ Salah replied and ran quickly

towards the kitchen, and came back holding a glass of water

which he gave to his father with a straight hand.

chapters.html:
— صفحة 21 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿20﴾

The father noticed that the hand was sound and free from

any harm or defect, and he thought to himself that it must

be the other hand that was hurt, so he said to his son, ‘Give

it to me with the other hand, son.’

The little boy passed the glass of water from one hand to

the other, and again held it out towards his father, saying,

‘Here it is, father… take it, please.’ How strange! The little

boy had also extended the other hand so easily… and it was

quite straight.

Was it possible? Had the afflicted hand truly recovered?

To ascertain what he had seen with his own eyes, the

merciful father virtually leaped at his son and held what he

thought to be the deformed hand. He examined it from all

sides… then stretched it out to its normal length and laid

his own hand over it. But this was all very strange… the

day before, the little boy was unable to stretch his hand

out… so what had happened?

Was it possible? Had the hand really returned to its

normal shape and was it now functioning perfectly without

showing any sign of imperfection?

But could the noble master possibly have mistaken the

damaged hand for the sound one?

He dropped the hand he was holding and took up the

other one and began to examine it minutely, just as he had

done with the first.

Truly wondrous! Both hands seemed to be perfectly

sound and active! There and then, the merciful father felt

— صفحة 22 —

The True Benefits of Almsgiving ﴿21﴾

himself in the seventh heaven and turned to God to offer

his wholehearted praise and gratitude.

He recalled how the doctors decided that not only was

this case incurable but there was no hope for even the

slightest improvement.

But how did this miracle happen? He looked at his son’s

face and asked, ‘But how did your hand become straight

again, Salah?’

The little boy replied, ‘Oh… Daddy, didn’t you see the

man who visited us during the night? He was wearing white

clothes from head to toe; he came to me and said, “Let me

hold your hand, Salah.”

‘ “Oh… no, sir, please, I cannot move it; it hurts me,” I

answered, and begged him not to touch my hand.

‘But he insisted, “Do not worry, let me hold it.”

‘He took my hand and said, “By God’s Will there will

be no harm in it.” He spread it out and stroked it with his

hand while mentioning the Name of Al’lah.

‘He did it like this, father,’ said Salah, as he imitated the

way the man had stroked his hand.

‘Oh, Daddy,’ the boy continued, ‘as soon as he put his

hand on mine and stretched it I felt that it had been cured

and returned to normal.’

In fact, the boy was relating the details of a dream he

had when he was asleep but he thought it was something

that actually had taken place in reality. This was why he

asked his father if he had seen the man or not.

— صفحة 23 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿22﴾

When the sun rose and the morning light spread its gentle

rays all over the universe, the father quickly donned his

outdoor clothes and told his son to do the same; then they

both left the house heading for the National Hospital.

They went straight to the office of the head doctor who

was surprised by the visit of his old friend. The doctor

thought that the merciful father still had a hope that medical

knowledge might cure his son and that he wanted his help to

make further tests.

The doctor addressed the noble master saying, ‘Oh, Bey!

By God, we can do nothing for your son. His case is no doubt

incurable. You are so dear to me for we spent our childhood

days living in the same quarter, and enjoyed wonderful times

together. And because of the deep affection I have for you, I

consider your son my son. So believe me, if I knew that there

was the possibility of an effective treatment, whether in

America, Russia, France or any other country, I would have

sent him there by air without any delay.’

‘But doctor… ‘ the noble master said to his friend, ‘I

have not come here for my son to be treated, I have come

to show you that his hand has been cured by God’s Favour

and Grace and there’s no longer anything wrong with it.’

On hearing these unbelievable words, Dr. Nazmi looked

in amazement at the face of his friend for he was shocked at

hearing his most beloved friend saying what was, in his

belief, unattainable. He could not hide his affection for his

dear friend and his tears flowed abundantly down his cheeks.

— صفحة 24 —

The True Benefits of Almsgiving ﴿23﴾

The doctor thought that his friend Mohammad Emin

could not bear the calamity that had befallen his son and so

because of his deep grief he had become mentally disturbed,

and was suffering from a state of spiritual disorder. This

caused the doctor to become deeply affected by the state of

his friend and so his tears flowed while he thought to

himself, ‘Oh, my poor friend… may God soothe your

distress and help you regain your senses. May He grant you

forbearance for what He willed and judged to be right for

your son.’

Having noticed the tears flowing from the doctor’s eyes,

the noble master understood exactly what was running

through his head… and then his voice rang out around the

room, ‘Doctor, I am still in my right senses, I haven’t lost

my mind. Here is my son, come on… examine his hand

yourself.

‘Your human medical science judged that it was impossible

for my son’s hand to be cured; as for the medicine of our

master Mohammad (cpth) it does not confess impossibilities.

Yes, indeed, the Master of all Creation has cured my son and

here he is standing before you, you can verify what I say for

yourself.’

The doctor moved towards the little boy but still

doubting and disbelieving the words of his friend. He bent

down and held the child’s hand which, as he remembered,

was afflicted one and then he began to examine it. He found

it intact; he moved it up and down, stretched it and bent it,

and in all movements it reacted normally and perfectly.

— صفحة 25 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿24﴾

He thought, ‘Is it possible? This is not just a question of

improvement, but it’s a perfect cure!’

But again doubts crept to his mind that he might have

mistaken the injured hand for the uninjured one; therefore

he took the other hand and began to examine it, but he

found it just like the first hand… sound and normal.

‘Oh my God, it is really a miracle but how did this

happen?’The doctor stood up stupefied by what he had

seen with his own eyes, and touched with his own hands.

He rushed towards the phone and called for an

emergency meeting with all the doctors in the hospital,

excluding those who had surgeries at that time. When the

procession of doctors came into the room, the head of the

hospital addressed them saying, ‘I want to consult with you

about the case of the little boy, Salah… I think you still

remember him. I want to ask if there is any possibility that

his hand could be cured, or if there is any way to offer him

medical treatment so that his hand may be healed or at least

might improve.’

The doctors recognised Salah and remembered well his

condition when he had come the day before. So, the doctors

who were specialists in this field immediately replied, ‘No sir,

there is absolutely no way. This is an incurable case and it is

impossible for it even to attain any degree of improvement.’

‘But… doctors,’ Dr. Nazmi said, ‘the impossible has

become possible, and this boy’s hand has been fully cured.’

The doctors looked at their chief with eyes opened wide

in surprise, expressing their denial of what they had just

— صفحة 26 —

The True Benefits of Almsgiving ﴿25﴾

heard; but just as their chief had done before they came in,

one by one they approached the little boy and examined

both of his hands until they all were assured that the harmed

hand had been cured truly and perfectly, and returned to its

normal condition.

There was but a single thought that passed through the

minds of all the doctors present, ‘Is this believable? The

hand has become sound and active once again as if there

was nothing wrong with it. But how did this happen when

the combined medical knowledge of doctors from all parts

of the world could offer no treatment and not even one

degree of improvement for such a case?’

They asked the noble master to tell them how this miracle

had happened. Willingly, he informed them how he had

acted in accordance with the noble saying of God’s Envoy

about almsgiving, and that this was the secret behind the

cure of his beloved son’s hand.

This amazing event was published in detail in a well-

known daily journal of that time, called al-Ayyam.

True, indeed, are the noble sayings of the Envoy of God

(cpth).

— صفحة 27 — ﴿26﴾

The Haunted House

ne day, Mohammad Emin Sheikho wanted to buy

a new house. So, helped by one of his relatives, he

was able to find a suitable one with the

specifications that he had given. But when he asked about

the price, he was astonished at the figure he was quoted. He

did not expect that such a fine house with so many

wonderful qualities would be so low-priced.

‘How strange!’ he said to himself, ‘It’s a typical Arabian

house with a spacious courtyard with water flowing from a

fountain in the centre. It has many large rooms; fresh air

flows throughout all areas of the house, and the sun shines

in for most of the day.

‘So, how could it be so inexpensive despite all these

advantages?! The price they are asking for it is less than half

of what it should be worth.

‘How strange! There must be something wrong with it

that I can’t see.’

So, the virtuous master asked, ‘What’s wrong with this

house that makes you sell it at such a low price? Come

on… tell me what hidden defect it has, before I commit to

buying it.’

— صفحة 28 —

The Haunted House ﴿27﴾

The owner of the house replied, ‘But if I do, you will

change your mind and won’t buy it.’

‘I shall buy it if God wills. So tell me, what’s wrong with

it?’

Reluctantly he disclosed the problem, ‘It’s haunted!’ said

the man.

He meant that a clique of evil spirits from the devils of

djinn-kind lived in the house. They constantly caused all

kinds of trouble for its inhabitants and made their lives

difficult, so they never stayed very long and usually left the

house soon after moving in.

Yet from his deep belief in God, our noble and pure man

knew that the Almighty controls and directs everything

justly, so he was afraid of nothing and cared about nobody

except God, due to his own impeccable conduct and faultless

character. To constantly seek God’s Satisfaction was the full

extent of his hopes and aims.

So, he decided that he would buy the house and accepted

the price despite the serious problem, and duly paid the

asking price to the owner of the house, saying,

‘Such a problem is not important. Here is the money.’

A few days later he brought all of his belongings and

furniture and settled into the new house with his wife and

family.

The day they moved from the previous house to this one

was difficult and exhausting, because of all the cleaning and

organization that it entailed. When night fell, it was not

— صفحة 29 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿28﴾

long before Um Fathi, the wife of Mohammad Emin, went

to her bedroom in the new house, worn out from working

so hard all day long and swaying from fatigue. She was soon

fast asleep and snoring.

As for Mohammad Emin, Abu Fathi, he went to sleep in

his own small room at about ten o’clock in the evening as was

his habit. He imposed strict rules on himself, one of which

was to sleep at ten o’clock in the evening and to awake at two

o’clock in the morning so as to perform the night prayers:

praising God and drawing close to Him, the Almighty.

With all family members deep in their slumbers, time

passed and the hands on the clock face slowly but surely

moved towards two o’clock. At the appointed time the

revered master woke up, but he felt uneasy… there was

something strange afoot!

It was most unusual not to find calm and silence

prevailing in his home at such an hour in the middle of the

night!

He heard the sound of an oil burner as if someone had

prepared and lit it. ‘What’s happening?!’ he said to himself,

astonished, ‘Is it possible?!’

‘Blessed be God! Um Fathi must have got up before me

to perform the night prayers, and then she must have

begun to do the washing after her prayers! She always works

so hard!

‘Despite all the hard work of moving house, arranging

all of our belongings and furniture, and cleaning the place,

— صفحة 30 —

The Haunted House ﴿29﴾

here she is… already wide awake long before the call to the

dawn prayer… as busy as always! God bless her! She has got

up earlier than me to attend to her duty to God and to her

family.’

He rose from his bed, opened the door of his bedroom,

and went downstairs to the courtyard to perform the ritual

ablution, and then to pray and perform the two bows of the

night communications as was his custom.

Actually, it was reasonable for him to think that his wife

had preceded him in his prayers and then begun to attend

to the laundry for when he looked through a window that

overlooked the kitchen, he saw a heap of washing and the

oil burner alight by the door of the kitchen, with a big

container filled with water placed on top of it. So, he was

certain that Um Fathi was in the kitchen!

He finished his own ablution, and then went ahead to

the courtyard, where he saw three young children holding

each others’ hands and jumping.

He found this extremely odd, and wondered, ‘Why are

children laughing and playing in the courtyard at such an

hour of the night? And how did they get in when the outer

door is closed and locked?! Really, this is a very strange state

of affairs!’

So, he approached them and asked their names, at which

point, the three children stopped, but still held each others’

hands, and then continued to jump up and down in a

lively, carefree way.

chapters.title: صفحة 31 - 40 (Stories of the Scholar)
chapters.html:
— صفحة 31 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿30﴾

Then, the oldest one said, ‘I’m Kberoon.’

‘I’m Azgar,’ said the middle one.

‘And I’m Zgeroon,’ the youngest said.

As soon as the third child finished speaking our master,

who was still puzzled at the situation, uttered the word

“Al’lah”, a word that came from a man who, through his

heart’s eye, constantly bore witness to his Provider, and

suddenly, the three children changed into columns of smoke,

leaving no trace behind them.

And then it became quite clear that there was no Um Fathi

attending to the laundry, no oil burner, and not even the

slightest sound or whisper. There was nothing but absolute

silence, and no sign that anything unusual had just taken

place on that very spot.

The virtuous master was most concerned about his wife

Um Fathi, so he rushed upstairs, barefoot, to check on her.

He headed straight for her bedroom, where he found her

deep in her slumbers. In fact she had been sleeping soundly

from the moment +she had laid her head on her pillow and

was still fast asleep. In fact it appeared that she had not

turned over or even moved because of the enormous effort

she had exerted and the fatigue she felt from her work the

day before. It was obvious that she was totally unaware of

what had happened.

Later, when she woke up a few minutes before sunrise,

her husband asked her calmly, not wanting to disturb or

worry her, ‘Did you get up last night, Um Fathi?’

— صفحة 32 —

The Haunted House ﴿31﴾

‘No!’ she answered, ‘I felt absolutely nothing, from the

time I put my head on my pillow until I woke up to pray

just before sunrise.’

Nevertheless, Abu Fathi continued to hide this event

from his wife for six years so that she should not become

afraid, due to any whispers or disturbing ideas that may

have come into her mind.

After that night, no more events of that kind occurred in

their home ever again, and the haunted house turned into a

house that was haunted only by the family’s happiness which

spread joy throughout, and which flowed constantly from

the spirit of that noble man.

So we learn that, when somebody rightfully resorts to

God and truly seeks refuge in Him, when they yield and

apply His Orders, and when they become truly upright, all

evils and offences will be driven away from them as they

will be protected and strengthened by the encompassing

fence of their true belief.

In this way, God will protect them as long as they stay

within His Bounds and constantly seek refuge in Him.

So, those that follow the right path will perform real

communication with God, and then the divine states,

enlightenment and witnessing will enter their spirits and

uplift them towards God, where they will become cured of

their defects and diseases. Then no man or creature will have

power over them, as they will have become clean and pure.

That is the state of anyone who truly believes in God,

for He says, “No power has he [Satan] over believers who

— صفحة 33 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿32﴾

put their trust in their Provider. He has power only over

those who befriend him and those who serve other gods

besides Al’lah.” ﴿1﴾

Truly, there is a great lesson here for those who wish to

learn.

1 The Holy Qur’an, Fortress (Surah) 16, The Bees (al-Nahl), verses 99-100.

— صفحة 34 — ﴿33﴾

A Vow Should Never Be Broken

ne day our man, Mohammad Emin Sheikho, was

sitting having a conversation with one of his

friends, when his friend asked him if he

remembered a certain mutual friend.

‘Yes, I do; what’s the matter with him?’

‘Poor man! He got married many years ago, but he still

does not have any children. He prays to God persistently to

grant him a child. But it seems that God’s Will has deemed

it fit to leave him childless. Although medical tests have

confirmed that he is sterile he has not lost hope. You find

him constantly asking God to fulfill his wish: he particularly

wants a son.’

This was how Mohammad Emin heard the story of his

barren friend who was, as he remembered from the past,

frugal to the point of being stingy.

Just a few days later, our benevolent man met the childless

man by chance, and as he looked at him he recalled his

problem. As for the man, who was fully aware of the highly

moral character of Mohammad Emin, his love of God and his

strict adherence to His Commands, when he saw him he

— صفحة 35 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿34﴾

immediately rushed towards him begging him, ‘Oh Bey! Oh

Bey! You are close to God and God listens to your prayers. So,

please, I beg you… ask Him for my sake… ask Him to give

me a male child. Oh Bey, please… I want a son to occupy my

time and fill my heart. And perhaps he will help me when I

grow old.’ As he was speaking his eyes filled with tears. Our

compassionate man answered him in a kind and gentle tone,

‘Dear brother! If you want God to fulfill your wish, then

make a promise to Him and you will find that He will grant

your request.’

‘Really,’ the man asked eagerly, ‘is it truly that easy? If

my greatest wish can be achieved by a promise, then before

you I vow to God that if He favours me with a baby boy I

will offer up a sheep… not just any sheep… it will be a

fattened sheep.’

And so it was not long before God fulfilled his wish. His

wife became pregnant within a few days, and day by day, her

pregnancy became clear to see. The husband felt as though

he were in the seventh heaven and spent the rest of the nine

months almost boiling with impatience whilst eagerly

awaiting the birth of his child.

For many years he had been yearning for a little boy,

and before long his hopes would be realised: there were no

words to describe the happiness he felt as he counted down

the days.

At the end of the pregnancy, the wife gave birth to a

healthy, handsome boy… indeed, some would say a beautiful

— صفحة 36 —

A Vow Should Never Be Broken ﴿35﴾

cherub that infatuated the hearts of all who saw him. The

parents were overwhelmed with joy at seeing their wish

fulfilled after such a long time of yearning and deprivation.

The baby became the sole focus of his parents’ attention as

their every waking moment was taken up with giving him

endless care and attention.

But what about the promise? It seemed that the father

had forgotten it as soon as he saw his beautiful baby… or

should we say he pretended to have forgotten it. So, he

failed to offer up a fattened sheep, or even a scrawny chick!

Miserable miser! Whenever he looked at his son and saw

him growing day by day, he became ever more loving and

attached to him. Alas! He had become immersed in the

favour and forgotten Who had granted it. He neglected his

promise to God and failed to give thanks to his Provider.

The highly esteemed master, Mohammad Emin, heard

of God’s Gift to that niggardly man, and he met him once

again by chance… although as one might realise, this

meeting was purely by God’s Will.

Our man congratulated him on his newborn son and

thought to remind him of his vow, so he said, ‘What about

your promise, my friend? Have you sacrificed a fattened

sheep?’

‘No, no… not yet,’ the miser answered, ‘but of course I

will certainly do it… yes, yes indeed… but not now. I will

have the boy circumcised first then I will arrange the

sacrifice… yes… yes, after his circumcision!’

— صفحة 37 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿36﴾

The baby was circumcised and still the father failed to

keep his pledge to God. For him to sacrifice a fattened

sheep would be a great financial loss even though he was

rich. So he chose, quite simply, to forget all about it.

Not long afterwards God created another chance for the

new father to meet our compassionate man who reminded

him for the second time, ‘I expect that by now you must

have fulfilled your vow and slaughtered the sheep, am I

right?’

Whereupon the man replied, ‘Oh Bey! Does God really

need my sacrifice? Of course He doesn’t. He doesn’t need

any sacrifices at all. He can feed all the poor in the world if

He wishes. So, He has no need of me or my offering.’

Our man became deeply disturbed on hearing his words,

so he said to him, ‘What are you saying? Do you think that a

breach of promise is an insignificant matter? I can tell you

that it’s most serious in the Eyes of Al’lah. How can you

back out of your commitment and go back on your promise?

Listen to me, man! I warn you, if you don’t sacrifice a sheep,

by God, within fifteen days and not a day more, you will

lose your son. He will die. You have made a vow to God,

and this is not something to treat lightly.’

When Mohammad Emin uttered these words he was

boiling with rage.

The man heard the force of his words which nevertheless

hid great mercy and fear for him, yet, unfortunately, he

failed to understand the gravity behind them. In fact, he paid

— صفحة 38 —

A Vow Should Never Be Broken ﴿37﴾

them no heed whatsoever, and he mumbled something

under his breath while backing away. He thought to himself,

‘Would God truly deprive me of the light of my life just

because of a single sheep? No… no, I don’t think so… my

son is in the best of health and a very bonny baby.’

Weeks passed while the child continued to flourish and

become more beautiful and active with every passing day.

Indeed, the boy could be compared to the moon as it

waxed day by day: Glory to the Great Creator.

Then, on the fifteenth day the sun rose in all its splendid

glory and was reaching its zenith as midday approached!

The baby was still lively and blooming, smiling at his father

and mother who took turns to hold him in their arms, and

breathe in that sweet, milky smell that is particular to

babies. They were enraptured! But suddenly the child’s face

turned pale and an alarming change came over it.

‘Oh God! There’s something wrong with him… it seems

serious… what is it?… what’s happening to him?’ his parents

gasped.

The baby’s face had lost its healthy glow and now

appeared to have a yellowish tinge, indicating that he may

be close to death, and his cries were pitiful as though he was

suffering unbearable pain! The parents stood helpless before

their child. They were looking at him bewildered and

confused by this alarming sight.

They sent for the doctor, but just minutes before he

arrived, the baby breathed his last while cradled in his

— صفحة 39 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿38﴾

father’s arms. The father moved him gently in an effort to

revive him… then he shook him, but it was in vain for the

baby did not respond. His bewitching eyes were still wide

open but his chest was still: there was no sign of life.

A long, loud lament issued from the father expressing the

bitter pain he was feeling at that moment, ‘He’s dead! He’s

dead!’ And he burst into tears. Then he remembered! He

remembered the words of his noble friend. He remembered

his admonition and advice. As his mind thought back over

the events before his son’s death he found that it was exactly

fifteen days from the day he had met his noble friend until

the day his child died!

He dashed out of his home and began staggering right

and left like a drunkard. He did not know where to go or

what to do. Poor man! He had brought this pain upon

himself. His feet led him inadvertently in the direction of

some of his friends who stopped him and tried to calm him

down. But he could only repeat the same words over and

over again, ‘By God, he’s a Prophet! By God, he’s a Prophet!

He predicted the exact time of my boy’s death. He told me

that he would die after fifteen days, and his Prophecy has

come true!’

As for our gracious man, Mohammad Emin, when he

was asked about his Prophecy, he said, ‘By God, when I

uttered those words I did not know what I was saying. It

happened as I said it would… though I knew nothing

about it.’

— صفحة 40 — ﴿39﴾

Talking with the Dead

teadily and inexorably the Day of Reckoning is

approaching the appointed hour when all of mankind

will be called to account. With every passing day, hour

and second he is drawing closer to the moment of death and

the afterlife to come. And yet he pays no attention to this!

Nobody can know when they will die; nobody can be

sure that they will still be alive tomorrow.

Oh Mankind! Do you not think you should prepare

yourself for this one inescapable fact: your inevitable death?

You will die and be interred in your grave, and then the

angels will come and question you. What will your answer

be? Are you making good preparations for this difficult

moment? What provisions are you making for this journey?

The Envoy of God (cpth) said, “Death is the best

preacher.”

Everybody surely has experienced the death of a relative

or friend. In our daily lives we are accustomed to seeing one

another, spending pleasant time in each other’s company,

and then suddenly, often without warning, one of us moves

on to the next life. This is a life so different from our present

chapters.title: صفحة 41 - 50 (Stories of the Scholar)
chapters.html:
— صفحة 41 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿40﴾

earthly life and lasts from the world of the grave until the

final world. The train of this person’s life has reached the

final station where it will stop and they are called to alight.

And so, they descend from this train of life, leaving behind

all those inside.

At this moment, they will come to understand that the

journey of life is too short and the relationships they thought

firm and unbreakable are now over. This is the act of death:

it puts an end to all earthly pleasures and breaks up company

and lovers. All the joys and pleasures of this life are nothing

but a mirage in a desert: people think there is water but, alas,

a mirage is nothing, and “nothing” does not quench thirst.

And then the fires of anguish, distress and regret are

inflamed in the spirit.

Those who spend their life in debauchery will come to

know the reality of their base desires at the time of death,

and then they will wail, calling for help, ‘Oh Lord, send us

back so that we can perform good deeds in the world we

have left behind.’ Truly, their sorrow and remorse for their

negligence of God’s Recommendations and for their loss of

closeness to the charitable Benefactor will be beyond

description. They will repeatedly ask to be sent back to life

in order to do good deeds. But, in fact, they are liars, for

even if God responds to their call, they will again fail to do

good deeds and will never change their wrongful ways. The

Almighty originally sent them to this world for this purpose

but they neglected to do this and foundered in the morass

of their earthly pleasures.

— صفحة 42 —

Talking with the Dead ﴿41﴾

In the pre-material world they neglected to keep their

promise to God that they would never turn away from

Him; however, God gave them another chance when He

sent them to this world. But, alas, despite the miracles with

which God filled this universe, and the warnings sent with

His Envoys, they take no notice of them and never study

them. And so, they are sure to fail again.

So, why do they call for a third chance?

They will never repent to God, and that is why they will

never again be sent back to this world. They will remain in

the grave, living in darkness, desolate and terrified. For

such people, it will be the time for regret and pain, and an

even greater terror awaits them on the Day of Resurrection.

In the Holy Qur’an, the Almighty says, “Give out of

what We have provided for you, before death comes to

one of you, and they say, ‘My Lord, if You would only

reprieve me for a little while, I would donate to charity

and become one of the righteous.’ ” ﴿1﴾

From time to time, and according to the depth of their

affection for the deceased, people go to the graveyard to

visit the dead who have left them. They stand at their

gravesides and read the al-Fatiha Fortress for their souls.

We greet them, and they hear our greeting and answer it.

They hear us and even talk to us, but we, the living, as long

as we are not illuminated by God’s Light, are unable to

hear them.

1 The Holy Qur’an, Fortress (Surah) 63, The Hypocrites (al-Munafiqun), verse 10.

— صفحة 43 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿42﴾

The visit serves as a warning of impending death for our

spirits. We, ourselves, are reminded of the moment of our

certain departure from this world, the moment when we will

leave behind all the adornment and vanities of this world

and be removed either to live in eternal joy or to undergo a

series of bitter treatments in order to heal our sick spirits.

For the spirit does not die, it only has a taste of death

when the angel of death draws the soul from the physical

body. Then the body becomes cold and no longer of any use

to the spirit. Therefore the spirit, which is the essential

element of man and his immaterial, conscious self, leaves the

body and follows the soul. By leaving the body, the spirit

experiences death as it departs from the present world, where

it was enclosed within a body, and goes to the middle world

where it becomes exposed, unrestricted by its body. There,

the angels will show it all the deeds and actions it performed

during its worldly life, as every last one will have been

written on its pages. If they were good the spirit will enjoy a

good condition, crowned with light, soaring up to the Lord

of Light, and living at the highest degrees of happiness and

joy. But if the deeds of a spirit were bad and evil it will suffer

deep sorrow for its negligence. It will be confined to its long,

dark prison in the grave, suffering loneliness and agony,

unable to escape from this dreadful fate.

We often stop to wonder: what are the conditions of our

deceased family and friends? Are they living in beautiful

Gardens, happy and honoured? Or what?

— صفحة 44 —

Talking with the Dead ﴿43﴾

Our great Envoy Mohammad (cpth) said, “By He Whose

Hand controls Mohammad’s spirit there is no home after

this world except Gardens or Fire.”

Who can know the state of the dead? Do you know

anything about this? I do not think so. Then who does know?

Indeed, it is only those who are illuminated by God’s Light,

those whose heart’s eye is opened to show them realities and

truths who know about this. And it was said, “Those

endowed with knowledge of God have heart’s eyes that see

what the eyewitnesses cannot see.”

Those people have certain knowledge; they look with

their heart’s eye and keep close company with no one but

Prophets and true men. This group is not found guilty.

Their spirits are free, not shackled by sin or shameful deeds,

rather they soar up to the highest heaven. This is because

they have true love for their Provider and are faithful to

their guide, the Envoy of God (cpth). They live and act

under his light (cpth), the light of the shining lamp. It is

they who can bring back the spirits of the dead. With their

opened heart’s eye they witness the state of their dead

acquaintances, by the light of the Envoy (cpth). Thus we

understand that their knowledge depends on certainty and

reality, not on doubt and assumption.

However, this situation is not destined for them, alone. In

fact every human being is capable of attaining the same high

rank as they have. But this requires them to follow the straight

path and avoid whatever is forbidden, and to seize

opportunities to perform noble deeds and commendable acts.

— صفحة 45 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿44﴾

The Envoy’s cousin, Ali (God honoured him) said, ‘By

God, when the veil is removed (meaning: when he dies), I

will not become more certain than I am now.’ While still in

this worldly life he gained true knowledge about what comes

after death, and so he witnessed the in-between world and

the world to come. This is what is meant by believing in the

other world. When a human attains this sort of knowledge

they will be able to talk to the dead with whom they were

acquainted during their lifetime. But the ability to talk to all

the dead in general, indicates a high degree of piety and

Godliness that is known to none except Al’lah and His noble

Envoys (cpth).

Our merciful man, Mohammad Emin Sheikho, took care

of his mother until he led her to true belief; and because she

was so attached to her pious son, she drank from him the

love for Al’lah and His Envoy (cpth), until she became a

pure and pious woman.

Through his humane and clever handling of his mother

and his honouring her, the noble master was able to drive

her heart towards God and help her to enter His Presence

while she was still in this world. And so, she lived in this

high state until she departed this earthly life, in a state of

happiness.

After her death, the virtuous master consistently visited

his mother in the graveyard to remind himself of the day of

his own death and to teach it that it must not pursue any

worldly purpose but seek only to attain God’s Satisfaction.

— صفحة 46 —

Talking with the Dead ﴿45﴾

This is a distinguished quality of a true believer; whatever

high rank they may rise to, they keep in mind that they, too,

will die.

Our master, Ali, reached a high degree of piety, however,

he continued to visit cemeteries to keep death in his mind

until he was called Abu Turab. ﴿2﴾

Our man, Mohammad Emin, was deeply affected by his

mother’s death and so he took the opportunity and began

to teach his spirit and give it practical lessons about death.

He would leave home every evening after performing the

evening prayer and climb Mount Qasiyun where the

cemetery of God’s Prophet, Dhi al-Kifl was located (and is

until this day). He used to walk up the mountain heading

toward his mother’s grave where he would spend the whole

night until day-break.

He had already asked the gravedigger to prepare a grave

for him next to his mother’s; and so he spent the time there

by lying in his own grave and reflecting on God and death.

He maintained this habit for fully six months and did not

miss passing even a single night at the graveyard all during

this time.

By such conduct, he practised one of the ways which

lead to firm belief in the life to come. For thinking of death

results in believing in the Afterworld which allows man to

become aware of the events of the world in-between and

the other world. Through this belief, the spirit will flow to

2 This is because a graveyard in Arabic is called turba.

— صفحة 47 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿46﴾

the other abode and live there. This is an example of what

is meant by realisation of the spirit; it means to experience

things through the spirit before they actually occur.

A few years before his mother’s death, our noble man

noticed that the house they lived in needed some repairs

and restoration of its wooden doors and window frames. At

that time he was an officer and a faithful follower of Sheikh

Emin Kuftaro.

So he talked with a carpenter who was, incidentally, one

of his brothers in the circle, about the repairs he needed to

carry out in his house.

This carpenter was a naive and good-hearted man; and

because he loved our master so much he soon agreed to

undertake the work by himself; and for many successive days

the carpenter worked hard and with great skill in the house

of our eminent man. He used to go there in the morning

and did not leave until the afternoon. While working, he

often heard the voice of Mohammad Emin’s old mother,

sometimes when she was speaking with her son, or other

times when she might call to him from her room or the

kitchen. Then her beloved son would answer her without

delay. Because the carpenter frequently heard the voice of the

old mother he soon became very familiar with it.

Then, a few months later, the exemplary mother left this

earthly life and her faithful son devoted himself to visiting

her every night at the cemetery so as to chasten his spirit by

lying in his own grave. For six long months, the venerable

— صفحة 48 —

Talking with the Dead ﴿47﴾

master continued to spend the night in the graveyard, lying

in his grave beside that of his mother.

One day, the carpenter missed the company of his

virtuous friend, Officer Mohammad Emin. He yearned for

his noble character and great integrity and remembered how

he had guided him to their honest sheikh, Emin Kuftaro. So,

he decided to visit him at home, but failed to find him there.

Some neighbours told him that they had seen his friend on

the road leading to the graveyard, and so he set off in that

direction.

By this time, dusk had fallen and darkness enveloped

everything around him, for electricity had not yet reached

our country. All alone, the carpenter walked along the road

until the way began to climb upwards in the mountainous

area, and signs of habitation were soon left behind. The

place was desolate; and with every step the carpenter took

towards his destination he felt his heartbeats grow stronger

and quicker until he began to tremble all over in terror. As

he approached the graveyard, he felt intense fear creeping

throughout his body until it controlled all his movements.

To try to overcome this state he began to mumble and

murmur, making different sounds to dissipate the solitude,

and calm down and put the exhausting thoughts out of his

mind. And yet all his efforts came to nothing! It seemed that

the night had truly drawn a heavy cover over everything

around him so he could see nothing but waves of darkness

which served only to heighten his feelings of loneliness and

— صفحة 49 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿48﴾

terror for his thoughts were dwelling on the place he was

heading towards.

However, his eagerness to see the magnanimous benefactor

was able to overcome such irrational and unwarranted fears.

The path to the graveyard seemed so long. He walked and

walked until he finally reached its outer boundary where he

caught sight of the gravedigger. ‘Have you seen Abu Fathi?’

the carpenter asked him eagerly as if something of great

importance had happened.

This prompted the gravedigger to reveal the secret conduct

of the virtuous man which was known to no-one but him,

and so he replied, ‘He’s up there, lying in the grave he has

prepared for himself beside his mother’s.’

The carpenter set out to climb higher still, to the top of

the mountain, and all during the ascent he kept calling out

for his friend in a loud but trembling voice in the hope that

he might hear him reply and his own fears be banished.

In fact, the distress that took up his entire spirit had

cleared all the other troubles that usually occupied it, and

with no interest in anything else in the world. His thoughts

were fully focused on one single matter: to see Abu Fathi, so

that his own gloominess and fears might disappear. Along

the path, completely deserted except for the many graves,

and in an atmosphere of dreadful silence, broken only by the

sound of the cinchona trees rustling in the gentle breeze, the

carpenter continued to climb while calling, ‘Abu Fathi…

Abu Fathi’, hoping to hear him answer at any moment.

— صفحة 50 —

Talking with the Dead ﴿49﴾

The august master heard the call while lying in the tomb

and he recognised the carpenter’s voice. He wondered,

‘What could have brought him to this place at such a time?

Why is he calling me? There must be a very serious matter

that has caused him to come looking for me!’ There and

then, he stood up and stepped out of his grave and answered

him, ‘Here I am. Come on, keep climbing.’

The words of the noble master brought a great sense of

relief and peace to the carpenter’s heart for they eradicated

his anguish and despondency and revitalized him. He felt a

renewed sense of energy and vitality so he continued his

ascent with faster, more nimble steps, with his heart reaching

out to Abu Fathi.

Finally, he reached the upper area of the cemetery where

the mother’s grave was located and there he found the noble

master standing beside it and looking at in his direction. The

carpenter heaved a deep sigh of relief at seeing his friend and

then greeted him warmly. After acknowledging the greeting,

Mohammad Emin asked him, ‘Is there anything wrong? I

hope that it’s good news that has brought you to me in such

a place and at such a time.’

The carpenter was still breathing heavily because of his

exhausting efforts and the horrible moments he experienced

on the way to see his friend; and his reply, when it came,

was with a quivering voice… , ‘It is only because of my

longing to see your noble face… I missed you so much.’

And the noble master said to him, ‘Okay, my friend, I’ll

come with you in a little while but only after I recite the al-

chapters.title: صفحة 51 - 60 (Stories of the Scholar)
chapters.html:
— صفحة 51 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿50﴾

Fatiha Fortress for my mother’s soul and take my leave of

her.’

Mohammad Emin turned towards his mother’s grave

and raising his hands he began to recite the Opening

Fortress (al-Fatiha Surah), while the poor carpenter stood

beside him reciting the same Fortress in a trembling voice.

When the noble master finished, he bade farewell to his

mother in a loud voice, saying, ‘Al-Salamu alaiki, my

mother.’

Everything was quite normal until the moment when an

affectionate and merciful voice reached the ears of the

carpenter that confused him and almost caused him to faint.

It was the mother’s voice, the voice of hajja Um Saleem

herself. He was certain that he had not made a mistake for he

knew her voice very well. He heard her reply to her son, ‘Wa

alaika al-Salam wa rahmatullahi wa barakatu, my son.’

‘Oh my God! What is this? I can’t believe what I hear

with my own ears! How odd! It’s her voice, her very own

voice! I still remember it exactly. It became imprinted in

my memory all during the time I worked in their house;

only a few months ago I used to hear her calling to her son

every day. But how does she talk to her son when she’s

dead? This is incredible… but it just happened! How did it

happen? How?’

The situation was so bewildering that the carpenter

became absentminded and could no longer control himself.

He said, ‘Am I still alive… in this world? Or could I…?’

— صفحة 52 —

Talking with the Dead ﴿51﴾

Immediately, he was overwhelmed by a feeling of deep

foreboding causing him to stand motionless, eyes and mouth

wide open, trying to grasp the matter and comprehend the

truth of what he had just heard. The woman had died six

months ago; but now, when her son greeted her she

answered him! It was the very same voice he had heard when

she was still alive! Suddenly, shaken out of his stupor, he

took to his heels, and began to run as fast as possible, as if a

malevolent ghost was trying to catch him and kill him. He

fell down, rolling over soil and stones among the tombs, as

the old mother’s reply repeatedly sounded in his ears. He

quickly scrambled to his feet and continued on his

downward path, going faster and faster.

His body was covered in cuts and bruises but he felt

nothing, for his entire attention was focused on one thing; to

reach the house of his uncle-in-law, Sheikh Emin Kuftaro.

He ran out the cemetery with the dust and soil covering

his clothes as if he had faced a violent desert sandstorm. He

kept on running as fast as he could until he reached the

sheikh’s house where he entered his face pale and covered

with dust.

When the venerable sheikh saw his son-in-law in such a

state he stopped talking to his guests and turned his

attention to the younger man and asked, ‘What has come

over you, son? What’s the matter?’

Puffing and panting, and in a tremulous voice, the

carpenter replied to his sheikh, ‘Oh sir… oh sir… It is Abu

Fathi… Abu Fathi, sir… ‘

— صفحة 53 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿52﴾

Sheikh Emin Kuftaro said, ‘What’s wrong with him?

Come on, son, tell me, quickly.’

‘Oh sir, he talks to the dead and they answer him!’

The news astounded the sheikh, so he said, ‘What are

you saying, son? Do you understand what you’re saying?’

‘By God, sir, I’m telling you the truth. I went to see him

at his mother’s grave, and before leaving, he said goodbye

to her and she answered him. I heard her with my own

ears. It was her voice, I know it very well and I was not

mistaken.’

Sheikh Emin found himself in a compromising situation

in front of those present; so to avoid this he said to the

alarmed carpenter, ‘Oh, son, I think you’re not well today.

Perhaps your night visit to the cemetery has exhausted and

terrified you. I think that you should go home to get some

rest. And I advise you never to visit the graveyard during the

hours of darkness again.’ Then the respected sheikh sent two

of his disciples to look for Mohammad Emin and bring him

to the meeting. When the two men went out to the street

they found the august master already coming towards the

sheikh’s home. Entering the house, our compassionate man

joined the meeting, his face glowing as though crowned with

an unearthly light that created pleasure in his heart. He

greeted his sheikh who thanked God for his arrival and

spoke to him directly, saying, ‘Come on, my son. Come and

listen to what my son-in-law has said about you. He claimed

that when you took your leave of your mother in her grave

— صفحة 54 —

Talking with the Dead ﴿53﴾

she answered you, and he insisted that he heard her voice

with his own ears.’

The sheikh’s purpose in informing Mohammad Emin of

what the carpenter had said was to let his guests hear a denial

of this incredible event. He did not want them to think that

his teaching was ill-founded and based on imagination. The

good-hearted sheikh was sure that the noble master would

answer in the negative and deny the event; yet Mohammad

Emin’s reply was quite the opposite! Not for a single

moment did the sheikh think that what they had heard was

the truth, and had actually happened. Mohammad Emin

said to his sheikh, ‘If my mother’s answer to my words had

such an impact on him, then just think what a terrible state

he would have been in if he had waited until I took my leave

of all the dead in the graveyard, and they all replied!’

Sheikh Emin was completely flabbergasted at the words

of the noble master. He was confused for he was certain that

Mohammad Emin was a truthful man, and he knew well

about his firm faith in God. However, not for a single

moment did he imagine that this man might have reached

such a high degree of belief and piety, a degree at which a

human could address the dead and hear their response!

With a look full of reverence and admiration for this pure,

godly human being, Sheikh Emin looked at Mohammad

Emin, appreciating his great love for his Provider and his

faithfulness to Him, a matter which uplifted him and led him

to this supreme dignity at a time when many people drew

away from God and ignored His Book.

— صفحة 55 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿54﴾

So he said to him, ‘May God bless you, my son! May

God increase your honour, my son. Indeed you are a

blessing that God has granted to us. What high standing you

have with Him! I have not reached this level, my son, I

mean, the level which enables a human being to talk to the

dead and hear their reply! Tell me, son, for how long have

you been visiting your mother in the graveyard?’

‘For six months, venerable Sheikh!’ the noble master

replied.

‘What! For six full months you have been visiting your

mother in her grave to delight her with the mention of God!

For six full months you have been spending every night in

the graveyard! That is enough, my son. You have achieved

what Imam al-Gazali did. Tell me, son, why did you do it?’

‘I wanted to refine my spirit, sir.’ Mohammad Emin

replied.

On hearing this, all those present looked at the noble

master with the greatest admiration and respect. They

wondered how, despite the bad times they were living in,

there was still a man with such noble merits and at such a

high degree of illumination by God’s Light, a degree

known only to Al’lah and His Envoy (cpth).

But this might bring a further question to one’s mind: how

could the terrified carpenter hear the reply of Mohammad

Emin’s mother to her son’s greeting?

In fact, the carpenter had been so overwhelmed with fear

that his spirit was completely clear of all thought of any

— صفحة 56 —

Talking with the Dead ﴿55﴾

other concerns he might have. He was wholly engrossed

with just one thing: to see our exemplary human being,

Mohammad Emin, and keep him company. The fact that

the carpenter’s heart was fully directed towards the noble

master allowed the carpenter to live in a state of heart bond

and spiritual connection with him.

And since the noble master was talking to his mother

and listening to her words spiritually, the carpenter was

able to hear the same words with his own spirit and not

with his ears as he thought.

This is an indisputable fact. When a spirit is released

from its love for this world, it will be able to see realities by

the Light of God. This “seeing” will be associated with the

senses of sight, touch, taste, smell and hearing: for the spirit

is the conscious self of man. In this world it is confined to

the body, so it is aware of its surroundings through the five

senses. It sees with the eye, hears with the ears, smells with

the nose, feels and touches with the skin, and tastes with

the tongue, which is also used in speech to express ideas

and thoughts.

But when the spirit is freed from its body and becomes

illuminated by God’s Light, it will see, smell, hear, speak,

and feel and perceive everything by itself: and this is

obtained only by God’s Light.

This is referred to in the Holy Qur’an when our Master

Shu’aib (pth)

3 talked to his people after their destruction. God

3 (pth) is an acronym for ‘peace is through him.’

— صفحة 57 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿56﴾

says, “Thereupon an earthquake seized them; by the next

morning they were lying prostrate and dead in their

dwellings. It was as if those who had denied Shu’aib had

never lived there: it was those who had denied Shu’aib

who were the losers. Shu’aib left them, saying, ‘I conveyed

to you, my people, the Message of my Lord and gave you

sincere advice. How can I grieve for a people persistent in

unbelief?’ ” ﴿4﴾

The same approach was followed by the master of creation

Mohammad (cpth) when he addressed the unbelievers who had

been killed in the Battle of Badr. He (cpth) stood before their

corpses at the end of the battle and addressed them, saying,

“You, people of Qulaib! Have you found the Promise of

your Provider to be true? The noble companions asked him,

‘Can these dead people hear you, Oh Envoy of God?’ He

(cpth) replied, ‘Their hearing is even sharper than yours.’ ” ﴿5﴾

Truly, in the character of our noble human being,

Mohammad Emin Sheikho, we realise the truthfulness of the

saying of the great Envoy (cpth), “All that is good flows

from me, and from my followers till the Day of

Resurrection.”

4 The Holy Qur’an, Fortress (Surah) 7, The Heights (al-A’raf), verses 91-93.

5 Narrated by al-Bukhari, saying no. 1370.

— صفحة 58 — ﴿57﴾

The Bus Conductor Is Caught Out

ohammad Emin was living in the al-Muhajireen

area on Qasiyun Mountain which overlooked

Damascus and its lush, verdant hills. It was

situated many kilometres from the city, so he occasionally

had to use the public bus as the means to go there and back.

One day, as he was accustomed to do when going home,

he got in the bus going to the district where he lived. Al’lah

had planned that after it began to move Mohammad Emin

would see one of his comrades who was also on the bus. He

greeted him, exchanged a few pleasantries, and asked after

his family and business matters; everything was as normal.

In the meanwhile, the bus conductor passed by them

asking for the fare. With good grace, Mohammad Emin paid

for three passengers: himself, his child whom he had taken

with him to help him in some affairs, and the friend. He

took no notice of what the conductor did after he issued the

three tickets.

When they arrived at the stop they needed he and his

son headed for their home.

With that, the youngster stopped him saying, ‘Oh, Dad!

Why did you pay for your friend’s ticket?’

— صفحة 59 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿58﴾

He replied, ‘I paid because he’s my friend!’

The youngster added, ‘But the conductor took the fare

from him too!’

Carefully, Mohammad Emin asked him, ‘Are you sure?’

‘Yes Dad, he issued an adult’s full-price, green ticket.’

Mohammad Emin immediately decided to follow the

bus to catch up with the cheating conductor, but it had

vanished along the road, so he accompanied his son home

and then waited for the arrival of the next bus in order to

board it and head off in the same direction as the first one,

to the terminus, but the two buses were going in opposite

directions: the one carrying the cunning conductor was

returning to the city from the end of the line, and the other

one carrying Mohammad Emin was travelling towards the

end of the line, so he could not catch the conductor. He

paid for a ticket to go to the terminus, then he came back

by bus and paid another fare to return again to the city,

where he found the tramway in the city centre, al-Marjah,

which was the starting point for the buses.

He stepped onto the bus looking for the conductor, and

when he saw him he grabbed hold of his collar with both

hands aiming to hit him. The conductor was overcome by

fear and began to beg his forgiveness, saying how sorry he

was for what he had done. Mohammad Emin then addressed

him saying, ‘Listen to me, you thief! Why did you do that?

How dare you take the fare from my friend after I paid it for

him?’

— صفحة 60 —

The Bus Conductor Is Caught Out ﴿59﴾

His prompt action enabled him to catch up with the

conductor and admonish him; through his customary shrewd

prudence he pointed out the error of the conductor’s ways

when he scolded and chastened him. He also took back the

money for the extra fare paid by his friend, then he returned

home on yet another bus. And so, altogether, he paid the

price of a third ticket for his journey home.

This pursuit actually cost him three times the sum he

got back from the conductor. Clearly his purpose had not

been about the money at all, yet the decisive factor and aim

were to stop deception for, as is well known, no-one could

ever fool him. He refused to be defrauded by the conductor

whatever the personal cost was to himself.

“I am not a cheat, nor can anyone cheat me.” ﴿1﴾

Moreover, if he left the conductor to persist in breaching

people’s rights, his misdemeanours would increase and he

would eventually go to extremes and become a force for evil:

he would become used to stealing and ill-gotten gains until it

became second nature to him. What is more, whatever has

been acquired illegally had better be treated by fire, so he

should be dealt with by the harshest measures, out of love for

him, and to protect him for his own good.

Through his wise behaviour and beneficent deeds, this

merciful man, Mohammad Emin, made an example of the

conductor and provided a lesson that would deter others;

1 This saying belongs to the venerable companion Omar bin al-Khattab: may

Al’lah be pleased with him.

chapters.title: صفحة 61 - 70 (Stories of the Scholar)
chapters.html:
— صفحة 61 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿60﴾

the conductor would be guided towards the right way, so

his spirit would never entice him to go too far and steal

again after this humiliating lesson, scandal and public

degradation.

But let us ask: what would the results of that transgression

have been, had Mohammad Emin not acted with him in

such a way? And what would happen eventually to the

conductor, the perpetrator of that deed, and anyone who

followed his example if they were never punished, or had

their lie exposed, and received a severe warning? What if this

unforgettable lesson had not been given to society?

Truly, if we were to be cowardly and fail to prevent

wrongdoing in order to curry favour it would generate misery,

pillage, robbery, mutual hatred and discord in this world

which would lead to hell-fire in the Hereafter.

Al’lah’s Envoy (cpth) said, “Let him who sees an

abominable act correct it by his actions, yet if he cannot

do that, then it should be by his words, and if he is

unable to do that, then it should be in his heart: but that

would be the weakest faith.”

— صفحة 62 — ﴿61﴾

The Distinctive Man

here were many invitation cards sent that day, to

invite a number of guests, prominent in al-Sham, to

a stately banquet to be held in honour of Dr Abdul-

Kadir al-Zahra’, who was held in high esteem in Syria. Dr

Abdul-Kadir also held the military rank of brigadier general

at that time. Amongst these eminent guests, there was a

certain man, distinguished by his handsomeness and

reverence that bore the scent of the musk of purity,

veneration, perfection and splendour.

The banquet was to be held in one of the parks of western

Ghutah where the weather was pleasant and clear. The cool,

fresh breezes evoked joy and gladness in the heart; and to

add to the pleasure of such a perfect day, close to the park

there were abundant springs and rivers of glittering, flowing

water whose gentle murmuring blended with the chirruping

of the birds to compose a unique, magnificent piece of music

created by the Hand of Al’lah, the Most Kind, the Almighty.

The crowd of guests arrived, to find a big table prepared

for them in the garden of the park, in the verdant shade of

the trees and close to the babbling waters. And though the

— صفحة 63 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿62﴾

sun was high in the sky on that particular day, its heat was

soft and gentle, causing no discomfort at all.

Generally, at that time, the western Ghutah area of

Damascus was distinguished by its pleasant, temperate

weather even on hot summer days, compared with other

parts of the county. This was due to the abundance of fresh

water and trees in the region, which influenced its weather

and resulted in constant coolness and temperate conditions.

The guests were smiling happily, and their bursts of

laughter expressed their joy and high spirits. Every one of

them wore the stateliest suit he owned, in order to present

the most elegant appearance.

The natural fresh fragrances of roses and various other

flowers mingled with the pleasant Parisian perfumes of the

notables and were diffused all around by the gentle breeze.

As for their voices, sometimes they were loud and sometimes

low, and at other moments they might fall silent.

But one particular man, the subject of our story, a man

distinguished by his solemnity, elegance and good looks,

left the other notables behind, and walked with his light

solemn steps towards the flowing water. The guests noticed

this but knew nothing about the reason for his action.

There, on the bank of the river, under one of the wide-

spreading trees, he took off his shoes and removing his jacket

he hung it on a sturdy branch of the tree, having first asked

the servant to bring him a prayer carpet. He turned towards

the flowing water and baring his strong forearms he bent

— صفحة 64 —

The Distinctive Man ﴿63﴾

towards the water to perform briskly the ritual ablution, and

then got up to pray in the shade of the tree. He had decided

to recite the noon prayer before he sat to eat with the other

guests, for it was time for prayer and if he did not pray at

once, the conversation might last a long time; it might then

be too late to pray before the call signalling the afternoon

prayer.

The assembled guests saw him and immediately

understood why he had retired from the group, and so did

Dr Abdul-Kadir al-Zahra’, in whose honour the banquet

was being held.

After some time, the solemn master returned from

praying to sit tranquilly with the crowd by the big table

where various small groups were conversing quietly amongst

themselves; but all of them noticed the venerable master

when he came back to join them.

Thereupon, Dr. Abdul-Kadir al-Zahra’ said, complimenting

the attendees, ‘Dear brethren! Prayer is not everything in our

religion… it is not the only support, nor is it the basis. The

most important thing is to have a pure, good heart and to

treat people kindly.’ Dr. Abdul-Kadir al-Zahra’ had spoken

these words as a courtesy to his fellow guests, so that they

should not feel ashamed before the honourable master, as

they were far from performing such a Godly duty as prayer.

When the solemn master heard those words, he

interrupted the doctor, a man of high prestige, not in self-

defence, as he was the only one who prayed, but to support

— صفحة 65 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿64﴾

the truth and to clarify Al’lah’s sublime Purpose beyond

prayer; for He did not charge us with it vainly, with no a

fruit to be attained. The Almighty’s Bidding to establish it

is not simply an order to worship, devoid of wisdom or

great purpose, but it is directly derived from the Majesty

and Lofty Wisdom of the Almighty.

He said in a loud voice, heard clearly by all the attendees,

caring nothing about any courtesies or formalities, for he

cared only for Al’lah’s Satisfaction, and the glorifying of His

Orders and High Statutes, ‘Oh doctor… oh doctor! A

doctor does not graduate from a stable.’

A wave of shock and a deep silence fell over the guests

like the silence that follows a rumbling earthquake. What…

doctor… stable…! Oh… how terrible! But the brigadier

general could find no reply.

By his words the great master, Mohammad Emin, meant

that had a doctor not studied at universities, he would not

have been a doctor, nor would he have received that

distinguished certificate and notable position in society. So

how can a man become good-hearted and well-intentioned

if he does not communicate through prayer with Al’lah, the

Source of all goodness, virtue, charity and perfection?

He continued, ‘The Almighty has not futilely ordered us

to pray, for prayer, in its reality, is the close communication

of the spirit with the Creator, and true prayer is like the

highest school of all the schools of heart purity, in which the

spirit is refined and polished. If man does not enter that

— صفحة 66 —

The Distinctive Man ﴿65﴾

school, he will not be pure of heart and noble of manners –

which is what you meant by your speech – and he will not

perform good deeds. And if that happens, it will surely be to

achieve doubtful aims hidden within his spirit. How can he

be a pure and good human being when his heart turns away

from Al’lah? He does not communicate with his Provider to
