attain that mark with which He tints the prayers who

communicate with Him; and who has a better mark than

Al’lah?

‘The master of the creatures, the Envoy Mohammad

(cpth), the most honourable man and possessor of the highest

and noblest manners, was able to attain that rank when he

surpassed all mankind in communicating with God in a true

heart communication.

‘Prayer, in its reality, is the link between the spirit and

the Great Creator, and its close connection with the Light

of its Provider. It produces countless effects in the spirit of

the prayer, which are greater than anything that can be

expressed by the spoken or written word. It changes man’s

morals and turns him into a man unlike any other man.

‘I shall illustrate this to your honour, by means of an

example: if we say that chemistry converts stone into clear

corundum, or coal into shining diamond, and copper into

pure gold, know that this is nothing but a symbol and a sign.

This is because true prayer, and true prayer alone, is that

which alters the hard, cruel heart – that resembles stone in its

thickness and density – to become like corundum in purity

— صفحة 67 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿66﴾

and clarity, and transforms the dark heart to become like a

brilliant, glittering diamond. It changes all of man’s qualities

and substitutes them with high character. Such is the

Making of Al’lah Who disposes of all things in the perfect

order.

‘Neither gold nor jewels are more valuable to the

communicant human than what his heart (spirit) acquires

of high morals, and gains of perfect qualities.

‘Our example for this are the noble companions who were

the most unlearned of people, but when they established the

way of true prayer, they became the best of people who were

raised up for mankind, enjoining what is right, forbidding

what is wrong and believing in God: as a result they raised the

esteem of Arabs above that of all other nations.’

In the beginning, when the venerable master Mohammad

Emin interrupted the doctor’s speech, all the attendees were

amazed, and they paid great attention to the solemn master.

A strange silence and great stillness prevailed in the place,

except for that wonderful, solemn voice which captivated all

minds.

All the guests listened carefully to his words, and admired

them greatly because the astounding realities revealed to them

and the high logic that they had not heard before, bewildered

the mind. Mohammad Emin continued his speech saying,

‘Prayer is the true chemistry that changes man’s morals from

one state to another, and the noble companions are true

witnesses and examples of this. If you really communicate

— صفحة 68 —

The Distinctive Man ﴿67﴾

with God… with true communication… you shall have a

light in your heart (spirit) which will be for you the strongest

proof. You will then sense it in your very depth and realise the

great change that has occurred in your character, that it has

become pure and noble, with no impurities to blemish it.

There will be no stinginess, no cowardice or envy, nor any

other qualities that are unfit to describe man’s character.

There will be only purity, chastity, courage, generosity,

nobility, sublimity, chivalry and honour.

‘And the more man advances in his prayer, and the strength

of his communication with his Provider is consolidated, the

more he will proceed in the fields of perfection; and I tell you

that God’s Favour is limitless and endless.’

Mohammad Emin continued his constructive talk and

superior guidance supported by factual examples in the form

of stories, and all those present were surprised, captivated

and content with that. He explained to them how to attain

such true prayer and showed them the way that each man

should follow in order to reach that level of prayer, and

communicate truly with Al’lah. This was the way of our

master, Abraham, that is, to think thoroughly about God’s

Creation and the signs of the universe.

All the attendees listened to Mohammad Emin with a

strange intensity, and the one who listened and understood

his words most deeply was the brigadier general himself.

In his self, he dwindled before what he had heard of the

sublime logic which revealed to him facts he had not known

— صفحة 69 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿68﴾

before, or ever expected to find. He discovered that Al’lah’s

Orders are all of great purpose and they are not merely

Orders about how to worship, yet they are all full of sublime

wisdom, not known by most people in this temporary

material world.

Suddenly, that eerie silence was interrupted by the voice

of the host asking the guests to make their way to the table,

for the food had been served and was waiting for them.

Among the guests, there was a beautiful and fascinating

woman dressed in seductive Parisian clothing, and she had

been the focus of attention prior to the speech of the

virtuous master, Mohammad Emin. She was the wife of a

well known, wealthy Syrian man who held a doctorate from

France.

She was truly a woman of great beauty. She noticed the

scholar’s modesty, and how he avoided looking at her. She

also noticed his unparalleled boldness and heard his wonderful

logic; all this was in addition to his handsomeness, singular

sublimity and perfection. It was clear that she admired him

greatly and so tried many times to attract his attention by her

seductive gestures, but she failed. He took no notice of her

existence at all for he was fully absorbed in correcting the

doctor’s courtesy to his fellow guests, and clarifying Al’lah’s

sublime Purpose in ordering us to pray.

At the dinner table, and by Godly Arrangement, the

chairs of the venerable master and the doctor were side by

side, and since the invitation was in honour of the doctor

— صفحة 70 —

The Distinctive Man ﴿69﴾

(the brigadier general) he was offered the best kinds of food

and his plates were filled with the most delicious food,

including various kinds of cooked meat, chicken and fish.

The guests began to partake of the delicious food and the

virtuous master started to eat from the plate before him. As

for Dr Abdul-Kadir, he seemed very content and he greatly

admired Mohammad Emin, so he said to the attendees, ‘Oh

brethren! By God, all that this virtuous master has uttered is

true. Though, initially, I was upset by his words, by God… by

God… all that he has said is true and within the realm of

contestable and blameless logic. I have previous knowledge of

this honourable master, and I vouch that he fears no one and

pays no attention to any accuser when defending the truth.’

Dr Abdul-Kadir continued to speak, thanking Mohammad

Emin and praising him, and all during the meal he took tasty

morsels of the excellent meat on his own plate and put it on

the plate of the solemn master in order to honour him.

As for Mohammad Emin, he addressed him with words

that were both extremely kind and warm, and so he had no

choice but to eat what the doctor offered and adjured him to

eat, wanting to placate the good doctor, since he felt obliged

to make his speech in reply to the doctor’s courteous words.

Meanwhile, the doctor’s great interest in the venerable

master had not gone unnoticed by the other guests.

When they finished the meal, the virtuous master was

sated and felt heavy and lethargic because of the great

amount of rich food he had eaten.

chapters.title: صفحة 71 - 80 (Stories of the Scholar)
chapters.html:
— صفحة 71 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿70﴾

After dinner, the host suggested that the doctor and the

other guests should go to the al-Fijah Spring, to the source

itself, as it was close by, and they all welcomed the suggestion.

The guests mingled and took a number of cabs to

accommodate all of them. But that charming high class

woman with her coquettish ways did not lose hope and was

still trying to attract the attention of the virtuous master.

He, however, did not look at her even once, which left her

even more determined to achieve her goal.

She was truly infatuated by him and by his boldness and

wonderful words: the way he could attract the minds of all

the guests and turn their attention away from her. She

therefore seized the opportunity and followed him directly to

the same cab he entered, and took a seat very close to his.

The cab set off slowly, then accelerated towards the spring

crossing the charming Barada valley with its captivating

landscape, attractive sights and pleasant weather.

Her Parisian perfume pervaded the entire cab; all the

passengers, except one, had their eyes fixed on her fascinating

beauty and were unable to stop looking at her. But as for

that chaste honourable master, once she mounted the cab

and sat beside him, he, unaware of her existence, turned his

back to her, choosing to face the window to observe the

passing beauty of nature. She had failed to entice him yet

again!!! She had hoped for just one glance from him…so that

he would see her outstanding beauty that attracted the

admiration of all men… except his! But his eyes did not

— صفحة 72 —

The Distinctive Man ﴿71﴾

swerve for a single moment, intentionally or otherwise! She

could not believe what she had seen… but it was a fact.

This is the effect of true prayer on the heart. Its honour,

sublimity, purity and chastity embellishes man just as the

sun embellishes the infinite sky.

Half an hour passed as he maintained his position, while

she was beside him and about to flare up with rage… she

found him to be like a great mountain deep-rooted in chastity

and honour… so how could she ever achieve her wish?

Many years later it happened that Al’lah willed that the

beautiful woman should meet the wife of Mohammad

Emin. hen she knew her to be the wife of that virtuous

master of whom she had never met the like before, she

remembered the episode in all its detail, and related the

entire episode to his wife: how he had captivated the hearts

of all the guests with his high, logical words, and how she

tried many times to draw his attention, but she had not

succeeded in eliciting even a single glance from him. She

also related how she sat beside him in the cab, but he

turned his back on her. She continued, saying, ‘May Al’lah

bless you with this chaste, honourable husband of high

morals and noble character… in my life I have never seen a

man of such high morals and sperior qualities. All of the

other attendees were vile, they did not stop looking at me,

but he alone was chaste and honourable.’

And so, let us return to the story: the passengers

dismounted near the spring, and headed for the main

— صفحة 73 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿72﴾

entrance where the watchman stood to welcome them, but

he apologized that he could not let them enter without

informing the director of the al-Fijah Spring water

department in Damascus. He phoned him and when the

director knew of the arrival of those notables, possessors of

high positions led by the brigadier general Dr Abdul-Kadir

al-Zahra’, he said to him, ‘Woe unto you! Let them enter

immediately, for my post and yours are in their hands. No

one is allowed to enter except those dignitaries, especially

the brigadier general.’

The watchman rushed off to attend to them with all

humility, and there, through the sparkling, flowing, deep

water, the bed of the spring appeared as if it was no more

than a metre below the surface because of the extreme purity

of the water, granted by the Hand of the Great God: one of

His great Gifts to the people of al-Sham so that they might

thank Him for the graces with which He endowed them.

The watchman set about distributing cups of water to all

the attendees so that they might drink and enjoy fresh water

from its source. The virtuous master drank many cups even

though he still felt a heaviness in his stomach after the

sumptuous meal, but the strange thing was that a few minutes

after drinking the pure spring water, he felt a lightness, for the

heaviness in his stomach had been dispersed.

That carbonated mineral water, drawn fresh from the

spring, has an instant digestive effect which is gradually lost

as the reaction of the beneficial gases dissipates.

— صفحة 74 —

The Distinctive Man ﴿73﴾

After that, Mohammad Emin felt that he had regained

his appetite and could eat once again if food was offered to

him, as did all the other attendees.

So, dear reader, you see how great is Al’lah’s Mercy to

mankind! He sent them cold, fresh water from the most

remote parts of the world: the two icy polar regions, and

offered them sweet water free from germs or harmful matter.

Thus, whoever seeks to satisfy the Creator by any deed,

even though this act may displease people, Al’lah will be

pleased with him. What is more, He will ensure that those

people are also pleased with the person who performed that

deed.

This is the real life, a life of honour and sublimity to

God; otherwise it is worth nothing.

— صفحة 75 — ﴿74﴾

The Quarrel between the Leaders

of Two Districts Is Resolved

od says, “If two parties among the believers

have a quarrel, you should make peace between

them.” ﴿1﴾

It was common for each district of Damascus to have a

community leader to advise its residents on every matter,

however great or small. This community leader should be

characterised by his bravery, honour, knowledge and wisdom,

amongst other such attributes appropriate to this position.

At that time, the merchants and notable people of the

district were accustomed to meet at the coffee house to

exchange opinions, advice, or simply to chat with one another

in the evening.

One day, the boss of al-Salhiyeh quarter and his peer of

the Sheikh Muhyiddin quarter were in a particular coffee

house which they both used to frequent. They maintained

good and friendly relations with each other, and each one

had his entourage of companions who used to accompany

him wherever he went.

1 The Holy Qur’an, Fortress (Surah) 49, The Private Apartments (al-Hujurat), verse 9.

— صفحة 76 —

The Quarrel between the Leaders of Two Districts Is Resolved ﴿75﴾

But, unfortunately, a quarrel flared up between them in

the coffee house and the dispute intensified to the degree that

both sides were issuing threats: the situation had become quite

menacing.

The devil inflamed the intensity of the quarrel between

them and inflated the arrogance and obstinacy in their

minds so that neither of them would give in. The discord

and dispute went beyond words to the point that it became

violent. Both leaders were prepared for it as they were known

for their inflexible attitudes; and as for the escorts of the two

bosses, they were prepared to spring into action but could

not intercede unless their bosses told them to do so.

The conflict and scuffle became more intense until one

man stabbed the other… a severe thrust that resulted in him

falling to the ground where he lay motionless, bleeding

heavily. The moment that the perpetrator saw his opponent

lying wounded on the floor, he took to his heels with his

escort before he could be attacked by the men of the fallen

boss intent on taken revenge for their injured leader, who

had been rushed to the hospital. Here, for the reader to gain

a full picture of the potential severity of the situation, it is

important to state that each boss had more than 1500 men

at his personal command, and should the problem escalate

there was the potential for much bloodshed between the two

groups.

The news of the incident soon became known and it was

widely spread across Damascus that the two strong men had

— صفحة 77 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿76﴾

quarrelled and one of them was in a critical condition.

Consequently, fear and terror spread throughout the

community, the signs of which were to be seen clearly on

people’s faces for they expected the situation to escalate and

lead to a very unfavourable outcome. And yet, the only

action which they took was to indulge in senseless talk which

made the matter escalate to the extent that the two districts

began to prepare themselves actively and took up arms for

the awful, imminent fight.

As soon as the news reached him, Mohammad Emin

rushed to the hospital to take precautions to avert the grave

disaster before it could flare up between the two districts.

The followers of the stabbed boss had put out the alert and

called in more men and arms to attack the other district in

order to avenge their boss. They were waiting to see if he

would live or die; but in any case, whatever his fate, they

had resolved to fight and take their revenge to restore the

prestige of their stabbed leader.

Mohammad Emin, intent on avoiding terrible bloodshed,

had gone to the hospital where he adhered to the injured

boss as though he were his shadow, and began to take care of

him. He surrounded him with sympathy by day and by

night, like a tender mother, attending to his every need. He

also made every effort to draw the doctors’ attention to the

man, so that they would take the greatest care of him and

offer him all the treatment he needed. Most of the man’s

followers, and his family, noticed what was happening and

— صفحة 78 —

The Quarrel between the Leaders of Two Districts Is Resolved ﴿77﴾

appreciated our man’s favour and compassion. So, too, did

the boss when he regained consciousness and was well

enough to be aware of our man’s great kindness and support;

he kept it in mind that Mohammad Emin insisted on

keeping him company and never left his side even for a

moment.

Within just a few days, the boss seemed well on the road

to recovery and the doctors declared that he was now out of

danger, so he was allowed to leave the hospital after the life-

threatening injury that had caused a lasting scar on his

neck.

On the day that he left the hospital, no one knew

anything about the plans and arrangements which this boss

had decided on in order to take his revenge on his opponent,

but Mohammad Emin forestalled him and put a stop to the

“devil’s whispers” saying, ‘You’re my guest today!’ The boss

was surprised at this but he could not refuse the invitation

after the great care and extreme kindness so generously

shown to him by Mohammad Emin when he was in dire

need of both care and protection. So, the boss accepted the

invitation gratefully and, as he felt indebted to our man, he

accompanied him to his house. Yet the two districts were still

on a state of full alert and readiness for the expected

encounter as soon as their boss gave the word.

In his home, Mohammad Emin prepared all that was

fitting for his guest, the head of a district, then he praised

him, conversed with him and soothed him till he forgot

— صفحة 79 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿78﴾

about the recent shocking incident; and this outcome was

entirely due to the cheerful and tender nature of our

humane man.

In the interim, Mohammad Emin sent his eldest son,

Fathi, to invite the other boss to his home but told Fathi

not to tell him anything except, ‘My father has invited you

to our house.’

Immediately, the youngster went off to summon the

boss who was in hiding for fear that he might be killed. He

had disappeared since the incident of the stabbing and no-

one knew of his whereabouts except our merciful man, his

own family, and his loyal escort.

When the man who had carried out the stabbing arrived,

Mohammad Emin welcomed him with due respect, and

after he indulged and reassured him they proceeded to the

room where his antagonist was sitting.

As soon as he entered the room he found himself face to

face with his adversary. He stopped still, one might say

rooted to the spot… his eyes wide open in wonder… unable

to believe what he saw before him! Was it true, or was he

dreaming? He shook his head, but quickly realised it was the

truth, and that his antagonist was really in front of him. It

was such a great surprise that it would never have entered

anyone’s mind!

It was just as much of a shock to the other man already

sitting there and they stared at each other in grave silence, like

buzzards contemplating their prey. All the while, Mohammad

— صفحة 80 —

The Quarrel between the Leaders of Two Districts Is Resolved ﴿79﴾

Emin was watching them closely, his eyes full of compassion

and mercy.

Meanwhile, the stabbed boss did not know what came

over him. He was suddenly overwhelmed with intense

feelings of goodwill, tolerance and mercy; all the spite and

hatred were torn from his spirit, and his heart became calm.

He found his heart aspiring to peace but did not know the

source of all this growing tranquility.

At this point, he stood up and turned to Mohammad

Emin saying, ‘Is this what you want, Bey?’ And suddenly he

opened his hands towards his antagonist in a manner of

conciliation, and approached him smiling. So the other boss,

although truly amazed, responded to him in a like manner.

They shook hands and embraced each other. It was truly a

miracle that everything was back to normal between the two

leaders

2 by virtue of this kind and generous man, Mohammad

Emin Sheikho. Every long-held grudge and sense of bad

feeling between them vanished and was replaced by rapport

and friendliness. They opened their hearts to each other as if

there had never been any quarrel!

After Mohammad Emin had finished entertaining them

in the most generous and hospitable manner, he suggested

that the process of reconciliation should be completed

publicly for everyone to witness that all feelings of animosity

between the two chiefs had now gone. He then walked out

of the house between them, and all three were chatting and

2 The two leaders were Ahmad al-Rammal and Muhyiddin Milli.

chapters.title: صفحة 81 - 90 (Stories of the Scholar)
chapters.html:
— صفحة 81 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿80﴾

laughing in the most natural and friendly manner. Everyone

outside saw this amazing sight! The impossible had

happened! And they began to wonder if they were actually

dreaming.

How strange and unusual! But how had this happened?

Everybody had been expecting a big fight to break out at

any time. The threat of death had been hovering over

thousands of anxious potential victims, but beyond all

expectations the opposite had occurred! The three men

continued walking towards the house of the boss who had

been stabbed, where they entered the reception room. His

family and supporters were waiting for him fully expecting

to receive the order to avenge their boss for the knife attack,

and they were fully prepared to shed blood!

But here he is in the company of his opponent and not a

sign of enmity could be discerned between them: clearly

everything is back to normal! Needless to say, everyone was

startled, and absolute silence spread throughout the room.

They sat for a while, and gradually everybody realised that

the dispute between them had truly ended due to the

intercession of the wise and generous man who arrived with

them.

Life then returned to normal after the entire local

population had been on full alert and fraught with alarm all

during that period.

Mohammad Emin then escorted both chiefs to the other

quarter to complete the process for the peaceful settlement

— صفحة 82 —

The Quarrel between the Leaders of Two Districts Is Resolved ﴿81﴾

of the dispute. They entered the guest house of the other

chief and gathered there with his escort for all to witness

the miraculous ending of the trouble and the amicable

settling of the dispute. The dark pall and the potentially

great danger which had befallen them since the quarrel had

now come to an end in the most unexpected way: with the

ending of the conflict life returned to its previous state of

tranquil and peaceful normality. Thus, Mohammad Emin

stopped the trouble and saved the inhabitants of the two

districts from a terrible blood-bath, which would probably

have been worse than anything seen in any of the counties

of Damascus before, and he saved them from an awful

aftermath which might have lasted for many years.

Truly, it was a wonder of wonders that life became

peaceful once again without the shedding of a single drop of

blood and thereby avoiding the horrible confrontation which

would have occurred if Al’lah had not shown His Mercy to

them at the hands of Mohammad Emin, the benevolent

man whose prudence managed to save both sides from a

potentially disastrous situation.

May Al’lah reward him with the best possible recompense

for the people of Damascus.

— صفحة 83 — ﴿82﴾

The Prime Minister

e had heard about transcendence and glory and

that some soared up until they reached the sun,

then the sun raised them higher still and

acquainted them with Al’lah, the Only One, the Irresistible,

so that they witnessed His Supreme Attributes.

The man of whom we speak was swayed by appearances,

so he set about building a tall tower, placing stone upon

stone, wishing to reach the sun so he could be lifted to the

heavens. He sought glory and believed that he could obtain

it by money or stones or gold. He wanted to achieve

eminence but he did not believe it would come to him by

giving up his worldly desires and abstaining from whatever

was prohibited, and performing good and charitable deeds

in their stead.

‘How can I become prestigious if I am not rich? Does

belief or trouble provide me with power? And what about

people? Will they respect me if I don’t have millions of liras?

I believe in God’s Existence and I really do want to recognise

Him, so I’m going to ascend the tower which I have built by

myself and by my own wealth so that I may reach heaven.’

— صفحة 84 —

The Prime Minister ﴿83﴾

But, “That Home of the Hereafter We shall give to

those who do not intend high-handedness or mischief

on earth: and the end is the best for those who are

illuminated by Al’lah’s Light.” ﴿1﴾

He set about emulating windmills, constantly moving,

thinking that he would gain something. He did not realise

that it is the wind that keeps windmills turning and he was

following nothing but a will-o’-the-wisp.

Suddenly, he found himself beginning to sink into spiritual

darkness. The lowly life unmasked its brutal reality before

him, having previously been hidden behind a cheap,

materialistic cover.

Today, for him, there is neither daylight nor lamp. The

dream has disappeared as if in a puff of smoke, the money

has become useless, the yearning is over, and he will never

again be able to sit upon the minister’s chair.

All that awaits him now is a narrow place under the soil

waiting to receive his mortal remains, whereupon it will be

covered by stones, leaving him alone without light or air,

and far removed from the people he sought to impress.

Why do people not learn lessons from death even

though they see how it never fails to take away their friends

and loved ones? The Prophet (cpth) told us a truth well

known to him when he said, “Death is the best preacher.”

In fact, if we fail to think of death and not prepare

ourselves for it, if we do not bear in mind that that day will

1 The Holy Qur’an, Fortress (Surah) 28, Stories (al-Qasas), verse 83.

— صفحة 85 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿84﴾

certainly come and that every spirit will definitely taste

death, it means that we have nothing good within our spirits.

There is no good in a nation that fails to remember its dead.

One finds, these days, that most people do not like to

hear about death; furthermore, when they are obliged to

attend the funeral of a relative or friend they stay only for a

few minutes, then as soon as the corpse is laid in the

ground they endeavour to beat one another in their hurry

to leave the graveyard, and give a deep sigh of relief once

they are outside. As for the poor dead person, he remains

alone, soon forgotten, and far from their hearts. There is

nothing around him save darkness and loneliness, and it is

no wonder, for the person who fails to recognise his

Provider and to be near to Him, will find no companion

and no provision in the Hereafter.

In this account, we are going to read about a man who

supposedly lived a comfortable life, for he enjoyed all the

pleasures and delights of this world and did his utmost to

become prime minister. This dream stayed in his mind for

many years, and since he insisted on achieving his goals and

the desire to succeed fully occupied his spirit to the point

that it reached its very core and penetrated to every last

shunning molecule, God helped him to achieve it.

Had Al’lah the Almighty not fulfilled this man’s wordly

desire, its germs would have engulfed his spirit and

destroyed it completely. He would not have been able to

forget it or to return to his Provider. But when the spirit

— صفحة 86 —

The Prime Minister ﴿85﴾

achieves its purpose, the germ of that desire will gather in

one place, which partially frees the field of the spirit. After

that, the Almighty sends adversity and disease to that

intractable man so that he may make use of them and turn

towards his Lord. If he does so, Godly light will flow into

his spirit and purify it, but if he does not, the germ of

desire will remain attached to his spirit, gathered on one

side. It will remain so until the moment of death where the

torment of the grave or the flaming Fire on Doomsday will

be a means for the purification of the spirit.

The man we are talking about had achieved his dream,

but it was the last thing he enjoyed, for it was not long after

that he was overcome by a serious illness as the ultimate

warning from God before he departed from this life and his

mortal body passed away.

Mohammad Emin Sheikho and the former prime

minister were old friends, their friendship having sprung up

when both were officers in the Turkish army. Thoughts of

his friend came suddenly to mind, so quite unaware of why

that should be, Mohammad Emin found himself walking

towards his friend’s palace.

But on arrival he sensed that there was an air of misery

and heartache prevailing over the palace. He saw the staff

endeavouring to wear masks of happiness although they were

clearly distressed. He failed to understand why he felt both

annoyed and anguished when he entered that magnificent

— صفحة 87 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿86﴾

building. He greeted the doorkeepers and asked about his

friend; they replied that he was crippled and bedridden in a

room on the ground floor.

He was most surprised at this fact, not because His

Excellency was ill, but because the owner of all that glory and

wealth was sleeping on the ground floor which is normally

reserved for the servants’ quarters!

A servant led our man to his friend’s room, but even

before he reached it, he could smell a bad odour emanating

both from the room and from its occupier.

Oh my God! What misery!

Ah! Alas for men who have lost the two abodes, those of

heaven and earth!

‘Eh, it’s you, my friend! Welcome!’ whispered the prime

minister from his bed, as our man entered the room and

saluted him. His voice seemed muffled, as though concealing

strong feelings of embarrassment and contrition. He

remained silent for a few minutes so as to control himself but

he failed and began to cry copious amounts of tears: it

seemed that every tear was like a firebrand that fell to his

heart and caused it to bleed.

‘Oh my friend! If only I had listened to you when you

spoke to me about death and the ugliness of this life! But I

was just like a foolhardy child distracted by his toys, and

here I am now on the verge of death.’

Mohammad Emin remembered that this man had taken a

new, young wife. But this merciless woman had turned her

— صفحة 88 —

The Prime Minister ﴿87﴾

back on him when he fell ill and became paralysed,

whereupon she put him in that shabby room, employing a

nurse to look after him. If she had not been afraid that people

would blame her and have no respect for her, she would

certainly have discarded him like a piece of old furniture.

She then indulged herself in all the luxuries of an extremely

comfortable life and set about spending her husband’s wealth

for her own enjoyment and amusement, along with his young

sons, and all within the sight and hearing of her bed-ridden

husband.

Mohammad Emin could hear sounds of merriment and

dancing coming from a room on the upper floor. They were

immersed in their own burning desires and blatantly

disregarding all principles and feelings of others. They gave

no consideration to that poor man who was crying and

calling for his beloved wife, begging her to come to his

room. She, however, did not care a scrap for her old bed-

ridden husband who still thought of himself as a young man,

nor did she give any thought to his condition. Moreover, she

came down to express her aversion to him. She stood arms

akimbo at the door of the room, gyrating her body, dressed

in a shameful, dirty dress suitable only for a harlot, and from

there she said to him, ‘Leave me alone! In your condition,

what do you want from a lady? Have you got anything to

entice me that may make me kindly disposed towards you?

Here’s the nurse, if you need anything, you can ask her.’

— صفحة 89 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿88﴾

She uttered those harsh words with such scorn as if she

was talking to a sick servant or animal. She even expressed

her loathing and lack of care with a dismissive movement of

the palm of her hand as if she wanted to push him away

from her, saying, ‘This is unbecoming of the lady’s prestige;

you have nothing that appeals to this lady.’

The husband burst into tears, his heart broken, while she

turned her back on him and headed off towards her den to

continue the shameful practices which suited her inferior

rank.

It was God’s Will which caused her to ignore her

husband’s call, except during the visit of his friend

Mohammad Emin! If that sick man had been of sound mind

and had applied proper judgement, he would have made a

conscious decision to escape from his terrible predicament,

but failing to do this he continued to slip towards the

lamentable end he eventually reached. But despite all that

happened and despite the unfortunate circumstances he was

living in, his heart was still attached to his young wife and he

was constantly searching for her sympathy and care. He did

not realise that she was the cause of his sickness, and that his

suffering grew much greater because of his yearning for her. If

only he could forget her and turn away from her and turn

instead towards the Almighty God, he would have a chance to

escape, and Al’lah would help him to be healed of all his

diseases and cleansed of all his bodily and spiritual

attachments.

— صفحة 90 —

The Prime Minister ﴿89﴾

Alas! There are many men who are like that prime

minister. They come into this world knowing nothing and

spend their entire lives in error then they feel as if they had

never been given any assistance or provision. They fail to

acquaint their spirits with the Almighty Al’lah.

After shedding copious amounts of tears, the premier

became silent once again, his eyes focused on some point in

the distance but saw nothing, and he began to think over his

past actions in this world. He saw his evil deeds surrounding

him and seeming to encircle his neck like heavy chains.

He was unable to sleep; but if he did manage to sleep for

a moment or two, he soon woke up terror-stricken as if he

had seen a ghost or witnessed a huge explosion. In his

dreams he twisted and turned, trying to run away and forget,

but there was no escape… the body had become incapable

and the spirit was shackled by its own deeds and its distance

from its Creator.

The memories began to gather in his mind leading him

to reminisce about bygone times…

He had gone one day, by himself, to visit Mohammad

Emin in his home. He knew the standing of our man in

people’s hearts for he knew that after he had retired he

dedicated himself whole-heartedly to teaching the truth and

guiding people to Al’lah; so his circle of followers was a

wide group of men who learned from him and appreciated

him very highly.

Yet that was not the premier’s purpose when he went

there. It was not his appreciation of, nor his love for, the

chapters.title: صفحة 91 - 100 (Stories of the Scholar)
chapters.html:
— صفحة 91 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿90﴾

people of truth, nor was it his search for the truth which

drove him to that visit. He went there for personal gain and

a request that was far removed from the interests and

tendencies of Mohammad Emin. He wanted to use the

position and popularity of our man for his own advantage.

At that time, he was standing for a seat in the country’s

parliament, so to succeed and qualify for premiership he

needed a majority vote.

‘So that’s why you have come here,’ our man said, ‘you

want me to recommend you to my company so that they

vote for you. Okay my friend! Do not worry, it’s a simple

thing. By God’s Will, I will do as you ask.’

In return, the candidate offered his unstinting ability to

carry out any request that our man might make should he

become premier.

When it was the time for the lesson and all of Mohammad

Emin’s followers were present in the assembly hall, he took his

place in the hall and in the hearts of those present, as was usual,

for him to offer them his guidance. Then he spoke to them

about the candidate’s visit and his request. But he added, ‘It is

not for us to expose a person’s faults or mention his bad

qualities and manners except in two cases: firstly, in the case of

engagement and marriage, for it concerns the fate of a woman

honoured by God who has been deluded. Secondly: in the case

of the presidency, as is our case now, for it does a disservice to

the common good of the nation and the future of this country.

Accordingly, I declare to you that this man is a man with a past

— صفحة 92 —

The Prime Minister ﴿91﴾

and he should not win the election. He is known to be a

drinker, a liar and a sinner… ‘

He told them the facts about a particular aspect of the

candidate’s shameful character and disgraceful manners,

then he left them free to form their own opinions and come

to their own decisions; but knowing these men as he did,

he was sure that none of them would vote in favour of the

candidate.

And he was right! Not one of them voted for this candidate

since they took the pure and virtuous man, Mohammad

Emin, as the best possible example for themselves.

Mohammad Emin recalled many memories while he

was sitting beside the ailing premier, talking to him gently,

surrounding him with love, tenderness and care. He wished

he could find the way to his heart so that he might guide

him to the way out of his terrible predicament, but

unfortunately the man was totally preoccupied by thoughts

of his wife and unable to forget her.

He remembered the day when an ostentatious limousine

stopped before his house, then two men wearing expensive

clothes got out, headed towards his house and knocked on the

door. When he opened the door, they both bowed before him

in a most courteous and civil manner then they told him that

their master, the new prime minister, wanted Mohammad

Emin to attend a reception being held to congratulate him on

the occasion of his success and appointment to the high

position.

— صفحة 93 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿92﴾

Politely, our man asked them the name of the new prime

minister who wanted him to attend this occasion. And he

was most surprised when he heard who it was!

It was none other than his old friend who had visited

him to ask for his help!

‘But how did he win?’ he asked.

‘He got the majority vote over all the other candidates,

so the appointment was rightfully his.’

Our man bowed his head for a short while, thinking of

what he had just heard; then he asked the two men to

excuse him and he went to his room.

He had never cared for such positions for himself, or even

attached any importance to these matters, so he was not

surprised that one of his acquaintances had been appointed

to a position of such high standing. However, what made

him wonder, was how a man of such low manners was able

to win!

He looked at the situation with his heart’s eye: then he

looked further, and yet further still to encompass the greater

picture, and he saw nations in decline having lost their

defining characteristics, and nations moving towards the

abyss until there was only a hair’s breadth between them and

destruction, especially at that time when the Second World

War was causing widespread devastation.

Truly, “Time is like its people and its people are as you

see” and “As you are, so will be your ruler”. To elaborate on

this, one could say that the events that occur during any

— صفحة 94 —

The Prime Minister ﴿93﴾

period in time reflect the nature of the people: if they are

bad they will be faced with disasters, and the opposite is

true if they are good. Similarly, God will entrust good

people to a good and benevolent ruler.

Our man put on an elegant white tie that reflected his

appearance of the utmost magnificence and splendour, then

he went out and got into the limousine, escorted by the two

men, and was driven to the presidential palace.

The car passed through the wide, imposing portal of the

palace heading for the splendid reception hall which was

surrounded by a vast, luxuriant and well-arranged garden.

As the car came to a halt, one of the two men got out

quickly, and showing great respect, he opened the rear door

to let the noble guest alight.

Mohammad Emin got out of the limousine then ascended

the steps of the palace accompanied by the two men, and

walked towards the grand reception hall. The large doors

stood open showing the hall crowded with guests who had

come from all cities of the republic to congratulate the

fortunate man who had risen to that high position and

deserved to be the prime minister.

As for His Excellency, he was seated at the front of the

room, talking freely in a grandiose manner and smoking his

big wooden pipe, while all eyes were focused on him. But as

soon as he saw our noble man step into the room displaying

his customary matchless dignity and reverence, he rushed

towards him and received him with a hearty welcome and

— صفحة 95 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿94﴾

led him to sit beside him, all the while repeating how happy

and grateful he was that Mohammad Emin had accepted

his invitation. He introduced him to the other guests and

told them about the great favour that Mohammad Emin

had shown towards him and his important role in the

premier’s success.

The prime minister’s overwhelming reception of Mohammad

Emin attracted the interest of all the other guests and caused

them to turn towards our man with great respect and reverence.

Those who were present to offer their congratulations began to

wonder and ask one another about the man who exuded such a

powerful personality. Why should he be the focus of the

premier’s attention?

Mohammad Emin’s sole purpose in attending the

reception was to admonish the people there. They heeded

his words, and so his aim was achieved!

Such were the memories occupying Mohammad Emin’s

mind while he was looking at the prime minister and

comparing them with the sight he now saw before him: the

prime minister lying in his bed, weak and humble, near to

death. It brought to mind the sorry sight when, on the

same illustrious occasion, the premier ran away from the

hall, escaping from the mention of death in order not to let

it muddy his joy.

This happened when the premier was recounting to his

guests an incident that occurred as he was passing through

Istanbul when he was a young man…

— صفحة 96 —

The Prime Minister ﴿95﴾

‘One day,’ he said, ‘I saw a tall, slender woman, strutting

as she made her way along the streets of the city. She was

going from one boutique to another to do some shopping.

So, I followed her until she turned into a narrow lane where

nobody would see us.’

At that time, all women were supposed to be completely

veiled when away from their homes. Every Moslem woman

was obliged to cover herself from head to toe, and the law

was strictly applied in the Turkish state whose success and

superiority in the past was based on its strict abidance by

the laws of the religions that adhered to God’s Statutes.

‘Then, I began to whistle softly to her,’ the prime minister

continued, ‘so that I might attract her heart, and actually she

turned towards me and uncovered her face! But what a great

shock I got! That evil woman thought that she could draw my

admiration and captivate my heart, so she unveiled her face,

laughed, and said to me, “Have I caught your fancy?”

‘She was a negress with a wide mouth and thick red lips;

and compared to the darkness of her skin, her teeth seemed

snow-white.… then she poked out her red tongue in a

seductive manner. When I saw her face, my desire vanished

and I felt myself about to black out, so I spat on the ground

and shouted at her, “Shame on you, you black woman! I

have wasted two and a half hours of my time chasing you

and you’re a negress.” ’

He regretted the time he had wasted in following her,

panting, priding himself on how clever he was.

— صفحة 97 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿96﴾

But the truth is that he was a blind-hearted man. He

distinguished between a black and a white person even though

Islam makes no distinction between them except according to

their level of piety and devotion to God.

This bad story appealed to those present so they began to

laugh loudly, knowing nothing about how sordid it truly was.

There was only one man among them who could perceive the

depth of the matter and because of his tender heart he could

not remain silent. So, he seized the opportunity and raised his

hand to stop the farce. He began to talk seriously, using

forceful and effective words to show the ugliness of this world.

It was Mohammad Emin who said, ‘Such is this worldly life,

my friend. We live in it seeking its material goods, ornaments

and pleasures. We even compete with one another wishing to

have the greatest share of wealth and enjoyment. We may sell

out our principles and compassion for its sake, and give up

our pledges and honour just to get a plaything that attracted

our hearts and minds. But suddenly death knocks at our doors

and snatches us one after the other, and then we will come

face to face with a bitter and painful fact.

‘We shall then see that we have missed all that is of

importance.

‘There will be no friends, no money, and not even any

desires. There will be only a dark deed that follows us and

clings to us like a shadow.

‘People are sleeping; when they die they will wake up.’

‘What? What do you say? Death?’… the premier said

fearfully. ‘Please, my friend, please do not mention this

— صفحة 98 —

The Prime Minister ﴿97﴾

word before me at this gathering. I do not want to hear it

and I hope that you will not mention it ever again. I think

I’ll faint if I hear any reference to death.’

Then he put the palm of his hand on the mouth of the

honest man, Mohammad Emin, trying to prevent him from

warning of death and the Day of Resurrection, yet our man

removed it and continued his speech. When the premier

failed to change the subject of Mohammad Emin’s speech,

he could do nothing but run away from the hall leaving all

the guests there; at that moment he cared nothing about the

prestige of his new portfolio, while Mohammad Emin

continued with his admonitions and illustration.

Since the premier was an old man his body had taken on

the appearance of a large jar with a short neck and round

puffy belly, so the sight of him running away was very

amusing: in order not to hear about death he inadvertently

made a comic spectacle of himself, which made all the

guests laugh at him.

What a wonder! Did that premier think that he would

live forever? Did he think that he could escape from death?

Or perhaps he imagined that the day of death was as far

from him as a star from the earth! The Almighty God says,

“Wherever you are, death will find you, even if you are

hiding in tall, fortified towers!” ﴿2﴾

So, after the storm of laughter and disparagement

quietened down, Mohammad Emin returned to his speech

2 The Holy Qur’an, Fortress (Surah) 4, Women (al-Nisa’), verse 78.

— صفحة 99 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿98﴾

about death, and they were all then prepared to listen to him

carefully, and were affected deeply by his ensuing words.

Their spirits turned fully towards him because of the

solemnity and dignity they felt emanating from him,

especially when he did not respond to the prime minister who

wanted him to change the subject into one that was pleasant

for him.

How can he remain silent when he is fully aware of the

consequences of following those desires and material things?

How can he keep silent when he knows well that those who

adopt a life of ease and pleasure are moving towards a dead

end where darkness surrounds them and fills their spirits

with rancour and delusion?

He cannot leave them to go astray without trying to help

them and guide them towards the right path which would

offer them peace and safety, and secure for them honour

and bliss during their lifetime, and then after their death.

He is not the one who refrains from doing good, nor does

he lag in seeking God’s Satisfaction and serving His

creatures.

Now let us return to His Excellency, the premier, so as

to recognise his mental condition after he left the hall. We

will see him regretting his behaviour which had caused him

to lose some of his prestige and eminence. He thought

about what had happened and saw the fault clear before his

eyes. He found that his actions were foolish and imprudent,

therefore he decided to return in order to apologise to his

friend and to his guests.

— صفحة 100 —

The Prime Minister ﴿99﴾

So, he screwed up his courage and displayed firmness and

dignity as he boldly entered the hall in order to regain the

respect of those present. He sat in his chair then apologized

to the noble guest, Mohammad Emin. He explained to him

in the presence of all the other guests that he ran out without

thinking because he feared death, and the mere mention of it

upset him. He was so afraid that he felt goose flesh on his

arms and his heart would beat rapidly whenever he had to

drive by the graveyard and saw the myrtle which was usually

placed on the graves. He would then spend the entire day in

a bad mood and unable to sleep a wink all during the night.

‘There is nothing except my life here on this earth so I

want to enjoy it to the full. I do not care about what may

come after death, in fact I do not think that I will be

resurrected. But what kind of fate shall I face if there is to

be an account? I don’t want to think of that.’

And now is the end! The prime minister became incapable

of enjoying any pleasure, and here he is lying on his bed like a

mosquito that has sucked a surfeit of blood. The worldly life

has turned its bright face away from him, only to replace it

with the other face which is terrible and dark. Today all his

deeds, all his possessions, even all his children are of no use to

him.

It was not long until the physical body came to the end

of its earthly purpose and the soul returned to its Creator,

after a death struggle that lasted many days. Then, he came

face to face with the truth,

chapters.title: صفحة 101 - 110 (Stories of the Scholar)
chapters.html:
— صفحة 101 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿100﴾

‘Where am I? Who am I? How did I get here?’ His spirit

seems strange and so does his body… the place is dark and

horrible. There is no friend, nor lover, nor child nor wife,

nor any other relative.

There are only chains and sins and deeds that cross the

mind and fragment. Today, there is no escape: there is only

a judgement of everlasting imprisonment with hard labour

that he brought upon himself.

Mohammad Emin had stayed beside him for some time,

trying faithfully to help him. He did all that he could in

order not to let him depart this life in such a state.

He wished that he could touch the premier’s heart or

draw his attention to him, his compassionate friend. He

stayed there waiting, perhaps his eyes might meet with his

or his heart turn away from its past, and then the premier’s

escape would be possible. But alas, even the eyelids had

surrendered to his shame, and there, on the forehead, the

stain indicating the past and the present was drawn.

Thus, the last cord between the premier and life has been

cut and the last glimmer of light has been extinguished. The

foundations of that tower which he built on sand when he

indulged in the hope of glory and immortality have cracked

and its pillars have sunk down to the depths: its walls are now

surrounded with darkness and the flames of hellfire. Now

nothing will serve him: neither hope nor repentance; and

nothing will bring him back: neither wealth nor servants.

God says, “The blind and the seeing are not alike: nor

are the depths of darkness and the light; nor are the

— صفحة 102 —

The Prime Minister ﴿101﴾

chilly shade and the genial heat; nor are the living and

the dead. Al’lah makes him to hear who wills; but you

cannot make those to hear who are indulged in whims.” ﴿3﴾

But in fact, the real death is the death of the spirit when

it turns away from its Maker. It is not only the soul leaving

the body, for life is but the life of the spirit: all of its deeds

are attached to it and all gains return to it, and the results

of the direction it takes will reflect on its surface. So, he

who turns towards the Creator, the Living One Who does

not die, and the Light which does not cease, his spirit will

stay alive, overwhelmed by the lights and enjoying forever

the Gardens of the Peerless Compassionate One.

3 The Holy Qur’an, Fortress (Surah) 35, Originator (Fatir), verses 19-22.

— صفحة 103 — ﴿102﴾

The Magician and the Needle

n the hills of Damascus lies a town that the Hand

of Godly Potency has endowed with captivating

beauty and all the most wondrous, beguiling

charms and allure of nature.

It truly seduces the heart and fills the eye with its

splendour. The weather is pleasant and clement, and the

houses are surrounded by orchards, thickets, gardens, flowers

and trees bearing luscious ripe fruits waiting to be plucked.

Such is the exquisite Artistry of Al’lah, Who has perfected

everything. A playful breeze wafts gently around the branches,

causing the leaves to quiver with the joy and passion and

refreshment that come from the diffusion of the refreshing air.

As night falls, all becomes enveloped in its soft, velvety

darkness and a gentle silence spreads over the land.

At one time, an Arab-style house stood here, in the midst

of farmland and orchards, and a gentle, welcoming light

glowed constantly from its windows. Although this was the

light of a solitary, simple lamp, nonetheless it contained a

kind of tranquillity, a heart’s ease, and a strange spiritual

purity, to welcome all who came to the house.

— صفحة 104 —

The Magician and the Needle ﴿103﴾

Inside this house, in one of the rooms in particular, an

unusual calmness prevailed. It was infused with a purity

and sublimity that never failed to overwhelm those who

were present.

A charming, melodious voice could be heard sounding a

tune, beautifying the stillness and sending forth an aura of

purity and delicacy that was carried on the air. A number of

visitors sat there listening with rapt attention. They had

come to see their beloved eminent leader, and to hear his

sublime interpretation of the Holy Qur’an, with which they

were fully preoccupied, and which filled their hearts with

bliss. These were the disciples of the great guide,

Mohammad Emin Sheikho. One of these disciples had

brought some guests with him, who had insisted that they

must be taken to see this virtuous master whose noble

qualities and profound words were the talk of people

everywhere. So, it was that when Mohammad Emin had

finished speaking, one of those guests – who had been

affected by an event that had happened many times before

his very eyes – said,

‘Oh, sir! I wish to talk to you about al-Gawi whom

people regard as one of the people of God. He has a kind of

supernatural power which enables him to know secret things.

Oh, sir! What he does is, he asks one of his attendants to

remove anything he likes from the room, even if it is as small

as a needle, and to go and hide it out of sight, wherever he

wants, without telling anyone where he has put it. Then,

— صفحة 105 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿104﴾

after he returns, al-Gawi goes out and in no more than a few

minutes he comes back holding the very thing that was

hidden! He is easily able to discover the hiding place and

bring the item back, even if it has been buried in the earth.

What a strange ability this al-Gawi has! Don’t you agree, sir?

He has become widely known, and the news of the

supernatural powers he displays has spread by word of

mouth. So, sir, what’s your opinion about such exploits as

these? And what position does he have himself? Surely

somebody who does such things can be regarded as one of

God’s people. Don’t you think so?’

With a gentle smile, the great guide answered him,

‘No, my son, he is not as you say. He is nothing but one

of the devils’ people. He performs such actions by means of

the devils with whom he has aligned himself. You could

also say that he is now nothing but a tool for them. They

use him to help them to achieve their aims and use their

wicked cunning to work with simple-minded people.’

As a look of astonishment spread over his face, the same

guest said, ‘So he’s really full of deceit… as cunning as a

fox! And he claims that nobody can do such things without

being one of God’s people and, what’s more, must hold a

special rank with Him.’

The righteous master said, ‘My son! If his claims were

true, the Envoy (cpth) or any of his noble companions

would then be more deserving than him of having such

supernatural powers.

— صفحة 106 —

The Magician and the Needle ﴿105﴾

‘Have you ever heard of the Envoy (cpth) doing such

things? Is there any mention of the companions performing

such deeds?

‘Listen, my son! Islam is a religion that depends on sound

logic and a righteous mind. It is based on acclaimed facts

and it is far removed from such foolish wonders. When the

noble companions continued the advance of Islam and

conquered many countries, they encouraged people’s hearts

and minds to adopt this religion through their rationality,

high logic and deep wisdom. They inspired people to cling

to God’s Book and yearn to assimilate the religion in the

same way that they yearn to smell the fragrance of the

sweetest perfume. Through this religion they were able to

clarify God’s Justice, Wisdom, Patience, Compassion and

Grandeur to all of creation until all hearts prostrated

themselves before His Majesty and His other Supreme

Attributes.

‘As for miracles, they ceased after the age of our master

Jesus (pth), for they served no real purpose.

‘In fact, people can gain no true belief unless they

themselves seek to ascertain the Existence of God, and His

Greatness and Kindness and all His other Attributes. They

should ascertain this through their own process of thought

and rationality, and by reflecting on God’s cosmic Signs,

such as the sun, the moon and the stars.

‘Should men be impressed by a seeming miracle the

effects will be short-lived and soon vanish; then people’s

— صفحة 107 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿106﴾

spirits will turn again to their depraved desires, and to

oppression and aggression.

‘Consider the people of our master Saleh (pth)! Did they

gain any advantage from the miracle of the she-camel?

Certainly not! ﴿1﴾

‘They even deprived her of her young, which made them

incur God’s Wrath. And there are many other examples, for

God says, “Nothing prevents Us from giving signs,

except that the ancients did not believe them. To

Thamud, We gave the she-camel as a visible sign, yet

they oppressed themselves with it.” ﴿2﴾

‘Anyhow, my son, you can bring this al-Gawi here and I

shall demonstrate to you his lying and duplicity, as well as

his worthlessness.’

A date was duly set for a meeting between al-Gawi and

the great guide Mohammad Emin Sheikho. The meeting

was to take place in the presence of the questioner, along

with some of his companions who believed that they had

witnessed great wonders and remarkable actions performed

by al-Gawi.

On the appointed day, the meeting was held before a

number of the disciples of Mohammad Emin, who

welcomed his guests cordially.

1 Those people asked their Envoy (pth) to let God bring out a she-camel with

its young from a certain rock so that this miracle would serve as a proof of his

true mission. But although God fulfilled their request they did not believe and

hurt the she-camel by hiding its young from it.

2 The Holy Qur’an, Fortress (Surah) 17, The Night Journey (al-Isra’), verse 59.

— صفحة 108 —

The Magician and the Needle ﴿107﴾

However, when al-Gawi entered the place, he began to

cast furtive glances at the great leader, looks that were both

towards the floor. He continued to repeat this rather odd

behaviour until they were ready to begin.

When everyone had taken their seat, the great guide,

Mohammad Emin Sheikho, began the discussion by saying,

‘So, what have you decided?’

The questioner answered, saying, ‘Sir! This is al-Gawi.

He has come to show us some of his strange marvels.’

‘Good! Then let him do whatever he likes,’ said

Mohammad Emin.

The look on al-Gawi’s face was still rather strange, and

added to this there had now appeared an expression of fear.

What a strange case this was! At first his face had carried a

look of conceit and disdain, but at this moment signs of

humility and inertia began to appear. He remained, as he was,

silent for some time. His face paled but his eyes still seemed to

be trying to focus on the great guide in a desultory and hostile

way, but strangely they continually failed to do so.

By contrast, the face of the great guide was clear and

radiant, His piercing gaze dispersed the darkness, just as the

rays of the sun pierced the dense clouds. He seemed to be

surrounded by signs of brilliance, dignity and beauty, as if he

was bathing in the Light of his Provider, living in a constant

state of passionate absorption in His Presence. A smile could

be seen on his lips, expressing his faith in the Provider of the

people.

— صفحة 109 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿108﴾

Suddenly, al-Gawi broke his silence, saying, ‘Today I am

unable to practise my work in the normal way because I feel

worried and absent-minded, so I cannot show you my

wonders unless the object is hidden by a female.’

Those present found this to be a very strange request.

They were accustomed to seeing him perform these actions

without specifying whether the person hiding the object was

male or female. So what was wrong with him?! Why did he

dare to make this odd request in front of the great guide?!

The dignified master, Mohammad Emin Sheikho, then

rose from his seat and went to his wife’s room. He entered,

and said to her, ‘Um Fathi! I want you to take a needle and

go to the end of our orchard. Go to the mulberry tree and

hide the needle beneath it. Bury it in the soil, but do not

forget to pinpoint its exact location with a marker, such as a

piece of granite or white flint, so that I can find it later on.’

She said, ‘Yes, of course. I’ll go at once to do as you ask.’

Mohammad Emin continued, ‘But I want you to keep

reciting the following Fortresses (Surahs) as you walk there

and back: Oblivious Humankind, Oblivious Jinn-kind (al-

Nas), All That’s Coming to Appearance (al-Falaq),

Sincerity (al-Ikhlas), and the Opening (al-Fatiha).’

‘I’ll do exactly as you say.’

She took a needle from her room and went up to the

orchard while her husband stood waiting for her to return.

She reached the far end of the farm and chose the tree

under which she would hide the needle. Then she put a

— صفحة 110 —

The Magician and the Needle ﴿109﴾

medium-sized piece of granite over the hiding place.

According to her husband’s directions, she kept reciting the

Qur’anic Fortresses until she returned to the house, where

she found him waiting for her.

‘I have done as you asked,’ she said, and then told him

where she had hidden the needle and described the marker

under which he could find it.

‘Very good! God bless you!’ the kindly master said.

He returned to the room where his guests were waiting,

and addressed al-Gawi saying, ‘Come on, al-Gawi! We

have done as you asked.’

Al-Gawi stood up and then went out to the orchard,

followed by the rest of the group. He walked among the

trees, and then stopped as if undecided which direction he

should take. Those present found that his actions up to this

point were not in line with what they knew about him

previously.

It was not long before al-Gawi turned to them and said,

‘She hasn’t hidden anything.’

The master replied, ‘Come with me! I will show you

where she has hidden a needle,’ and they all followed him

to the hiding place. He stooped to the ground and removed

the white flint, and then dug at the soil lightly with his

finger until the needle appeared clearly to the eyes of those

present.

Mohammad Emin picked it up, and turned towards the

sorcerer saying, ‘So, what do you have to say about this?’

chapters.title: صفحة 111 - 120 (Stories of the Scholar)
chapters.html:
— صفحة 111 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿110﴾

‘Let her do it again.’ said al-Gawi, ‘but this time, I want

you to stay in the room with us until she returns.’

The venerable master smiled and said, ‘As you like. Let

us go back to the house.’

Once again, they all entered the room except Mohammad

Emin who went to ask his wife to hide the needle again, but

in a different place that they both agreed on, and then he

entered the room and stayed with the group. Despite this, al-

Gawi was fated to face failure yet again.

They repeated the exercise a third time at al-Gawi’s

request, but he fared no better than on the two previous

occasions.

Thus, al-Gawi realised that if he had truly possessed

hidden knowledge, he would not have failed to find the

hidden object.

Therefore, he could only confess his failure, and so

became humbled in the view of all those present. He had

lost his prestige in their eyes, and especially in the view of

the questioner, who had previously been greatly impressed

by him to the extent that he had thought him one of God’s

people. However, in reality, he was nothing but a magician,

as the faithful guide Mohammad Emin Sheikho had said all

along.

A magician can never thrive in the presence of a true

believer that seeks power and refuge in his Provider and

keeps Him wholeheartedly in his mind, as in the case of the

great guide Mohammad Emin Sheikho. This is because the

— صفحة 112 —

The Magician and the Needle ﴿111﴾

magician’s devilish consorts will be unable to approach a

true believer, as light and fire cannot come together. When

angels come, devils run away! God says, “He it is Who

keeps communication with you, as do His angels, so that

He may bring you out from the depths of darkness into

light.” ﴿3﴾

One must always keep in mind that magicians can never

have power over believers who have been illuminated by

Al’lah’s Light.

3 The Holy Qur’an, Fortress (Surah) 33, The Combined Clans (al-Ahzab), verse 43.

— صفحة 113 — ﴿112﴾

A Wealthy Man Suffers for His Sin

nce, the owner of al-Khuja Market in Damascus

invited the elite of the religious scholars to a

banquet. When they arrived, the generous young

man welcomed them and received them with perfect

hospitality. The table was prepared and many dishes of

sumptious food were brought in; once his esteemed guests

were seated he asked them to start eating, but they replied

that they would not do so unless he shared it with them. The

host excused himself saying that he could not eat normal

food like them for his nourishment was restricted to liquids

only. They insisted on his eating with them even if it was

only one small morsel, but again he excused himself and

explained to them that his reaction might disturb them if he

were to eat solid food.

Because of their insistence he felt obliged to have a single

mouthful, so he tried to chew the food and then to swallow it

but he was unable to do so. His face became red and mottled

and his voice quavered so that he seemed to be suffocating.

He fell down, his body lying on the ground and jerking as he

gasped for breath: it seemed that he was about to die.

— صفحة 114 —

A Wealthy Man Suffers for His Sin ﴿113﴾

Within half an hour, the young man had recovered

completely and there was nothing to show for the

unpleasant episode save the pallor of his face.

When the guests witnessed the plight of their host they

were most upset and lost their appetite for the food set before

them. Among those present was our venerable scholar,

Mohammad Emin, who took the matter most seriously. He

thought, ‘As far as I know, this young man is good-hearted,

well-mannered and religious. He is charitable and is always

prepared to do a favour. So, why did God, the Just, the

Compassionate, send him this dire affliction? Definitely, he

must have done something wrong for, “No disaster befalls

you unless you have caused a disaster twice as great.”

1 Far

be it from God to be unjust.’

When the young man recovered, he insisted that his guests

should relax and eat their meal which, one must add, was

delicious and extremely generous. So, when his guests had

finished eating they thanked him for his kind hospitality and

generosity, then they took their leave of him and left the

house.

Apart from their initial reaction, not one of them cared

for the awful affliction of the young man except Mohammad

Emin who kept thinking of what had happened, and the

reason why he was unable to eat solid food. He truly wanted

to know what he had done to deserve such a punishment.

For the noble verse plainly serves, “What does Al’lah gain

1 The Holy Qur’an, Fortress (Surah) 3, The Family of ‘Imran (Al ‘Imran), verse 165.

— صفحة 115 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿114﴾

by punishing you if you are grateful and you are a

believer?” ﴿2﴾

Therefore, he befriended the young man for a long time

during which he frequently tested his character and true

nature. Every time he found him to be both honest and

upright, so he became even more interested to discover the

reason behind the problem; but it seemed that the young

man’s secret was too deeply buried. He kept it to himself

and did not disclose it; nevertheless, our man kept him

company and did not desert him.

It took twelve years for the young man to be sure of the

honesty and trustworthiness of our merciful man, and only

then did he unburden himself and disclose his secret. He said

to Mohammad Emin, ‘I want to tell you the reason for my

affliction: my father was the owner of all the shops in al-Khuja

Market. Although he was extremely wealthy, he was also very

tightfisted, insomuch that he used to feed us nothing but

bread. We begged him many times to provide for us those

things that all fathers provide for their children but he refused,

and in fact he became even stingier. He was ill-mannered and

treated us badly. Our life became unbearable because of his

evil nature. All my family, the old and the young alike, turned

to God praying that He would save us from the hardship of

living with him. One day, he suddenly fell quite ill and

became bedridden, so the physicians decided to perform

surgery on him. In fact, the surgeon decided to perform the

2 The Holy Qur’an, Fortress (Surah) 4, Women (al-Nisa’), verse 147.

— صفحة 116 —

A Wealthy Man Suffers for His Sin ﴿115﴾

operation at our house and had all the necessary equipment

sent there. At a critical stage during the operation the doctor

needed a particular instrument, but I had hidden it. He

looked everywhere for it and shouted at us, but it was in vain.

During that time my father took his last breath and died.’

On hearing this, our great scholar understood the full

implications of this serious matter and finally realised the

reasons for the young man’s affliction, after twelve long years

of research and investigation. He perceived that the Almighty

God had rightly deprived him of his father’s estate because of

this particular action.

Following this event, the man repented of the crime he

had committed against his father. If he had borne his father

with patience, his father would have left this earthly life even

if the doctor had not been missing one of his instruments,

for a man will die at his appointed time. It is not necessary

for anyone to force this issue by killing him.

The virtuous scholar, Mohammad Emin, always had great

faith in his Provider. He was certain that He is Just and

Merciful towards all of His creatures, so He directs to man

nothing but good and whatever helps him to save his spirit in

this earthly world before he departs to the other world; thus any

affliction that befalls a man is as a result of his own behaviour

or wrongdoing. The law of justice is in effect amongst all

creatures, for God says, “We did them no wrong, but they

were accustomed to doing wrong to themselves.” ﴿3﴾

3 The Holy Qur’an, Fortress (Surah) 16, The Bees (al-Nahl), verse 118.

— صفحة 117 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿116﴾

Our man became even more assured of the Fairness of

God’s Actions when He sent a distressing affliction to the

young man’s body so as to cure his spirit and to make him

serve as a lesson for everybody that lusts after money and,

in doing so, does away with his own sense of humanity.

However low and ignominious a man may be, his human

value is higher in the Eyes of his Provider than anything that

exists in this worldly life. So, when you strive against your

errant brother, let your reason be simply to help him return

to the right path and uplift him, and not be for the purpose

of acquiring his money, or for any other vain ambition. And

one should keep in mind that Al’lah helps him who helps his

brother with benevolence and compassion.

The young man eventually became full of remorse because

of what he had done to his father for the sake of money, and so

he decided to adopt the ways of righteousness and obedience,

and spent his father’s wealth in dispensing favours, helping the

needy and helpless, and treating the people of religion, and its

scholars, with great hospitality. No doubt, Al’lah the Almighty

accepted his repentance because of his ensuing noble conduct,

but as punishment for his spirit in this world He did not let

him, personally, enjoy his father’s wealth.

Far be it from Al’lah, the Just, the Compassionate, to

direct evil towards any one of His servants unless that is

what His servant deserves.

“And nor is your Lord ever the least bit Unjust to His

servants.” ﴿4﴾

4 The Holy Qur’an, Fortress (Surah) 41, Explained (Fussilat), verse 46.

— صفحة 118 — ﴿117﴾

The Young Housemaid

amascus, the aromatic garden, has always been a

great source of inspiration for poets. They wrote

and sang of the fresh sparkling waters of its river, of

its pleasant climate, fresh, gentle breeze and its beautiful

nature. Such was its beauty that they called it Al’lah’s Paradise

on earth.

Our story took place many decades ago when the Bedouins

who lived in its semi-desert region passed through difficult

circumstances due to a year without rain; unfortunately the

ensuing drought brought about great poverty and some of

them resorted to stealing.

During those years, Mohammad Emin Sheikho used to

lease a house and its surrounding orchard in a rural area, and

every summer he would leave Damascus with his family, and

head for this pleasant summer home away from the hustle

and bustle of the city. He used to spend the entire summer

there relaxing with his family and enjoy eating fresh fruits

directly from the trees of the orchard.

Qud’ssaya, is the name of this wondrous suburb and is

the setting for this story…

— صفحة 119 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿118﴾

Dear reader, let us spend a few hours with Mohammad

Emin Sheikho in his lush orchard, where the many trees

display an abundance of ripe fruits; the gentle breeze rustles

the leaves, we become aware that it is the Justice of God

that rules everything, and we sense the faithfulness of our

man and his great care to attain God’s Satisfaction – (Glory

to His Names).

It was a little before noon and Mohammad Emin was

sitting on his wooden chair in front of the house, relaxing and

enjoying the warm sunshine, hoping that it may relieve the

stomach-ache which was troubling him. While immersed in

his thoughts, he heard a low sound, so he turned towards the

direction it came from and listened carefully. Within a few

moments, a Bedouin woman appeared. She was tiptoeing

towards the middle of the orchard seemingly intent on

stealing some fruit because she was hungry. However, she

failed to notice the owner of the field, Mohammad Emin,

sitting by the house and she was startled when our virtuous

man called out, ‘Hey, you, what are you doing there?’ When

she heard his voice, she turned round and immediately ran off

like a frightened rabbit leaving the orchard behind her.

When she was out of sight he remained silent for a while

thinking about her circumstances. He thought to himself,

‘Perhaps she is hungry and has no other recourse and so her

spirit is out of control. I think that the drought in the

desert has caused the lack of food and is what has prompted

her to steal fruit from the orchard.’ Wasting no time, he got

— صفحة 120 —

The Young Housemaid ﴿119﴾

to his feet and hurried towards the oven in the orchard on

which there was a cooking pot filled with stuffed marrow.

He took a piece of traditional flat bread from the kneading

trough and folded several pieces of stuffed marrow inside it.

A little girl, about seven years old, stood a short distance

away watching what her master was doing. Her parents had

asked the honourable guide, Mohammad Emin, to employ

her as a simple housemaid, and at the same time they wanted

her to get a good spiritual education at his hands because of

what they had heard about his impeccable noble character.

‘Come here… good girl… quickly,…’ Mohammad Emin

called to her. She hurried forward and stopped before him.

He stretched out his hand holding the food and gave it to

her saying, ‘A Bedouin woman has just gone that way; come

on… good girl! Take this food and follow her. Hurry up and

give it to her before she has the chance to leave.’

She took the food and ran in the direction which her

master pointed to. She was soon back and smiling happily

as she walked towards him.

‘Did you find her?’

‘Yes, I did, sir.’

‘Did you give her the food?’

‘Yes, she took it and quickly put all of the stuffed

marrow inside the flat bread and folded it up, then began

to eat it greedily like this… ‘

The child was standing before our noble man, demonstrating

how the woman devoured the food… opening her mouth to

chapters.title: صفحة 121 - 130 (Stories of the Scholar)
chapters.html:
— صفحة 121 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿120﴾

bite the sandwich just as a ravenous beast might do… biting

off mouthfuls of food, swallowing, and tossing its head.
