Through the scene that the little girl was enacting, he

understood just how hungry that poor Bedouin woman

must be; and he thought, ‘How sad! She’s trembling with

hunger! Perhaps the food I sent her isn’t enough.’ He rushed

back to the oven and took two pieces of flat bread; he

wrapped it around many pieces of stuffed marrow then he

gave the food to the little girl saying, ‘Off you go! Take it to

her as quickly as possible.’ She held it fast and ran quickly

back to where she had left the Bedouin woman devouring

the food. She gave the second meal to the woman, who took

it and began to scoff it in the same voracious manner. This

was what the little maid recounted to her master when he

asked her whether she had found the woman or not, ‘Yes, I

did,’ the girl answered, ‘and she ate it like this…’ again she

imitated the woman’s manner of eating, shaking her head,

demonstrating the woman’s great hunger.

Our man pondered the woman’s situation. He was

concerned that she might have small children who would

surely be as hungry as she was. He said to himself, ‘I think

that she’s no longer hungry; but what about her children?

What about the coming days?’ and he turned towards the

little girl saying to her, ‘Come on, little one! Follow her

quickly before she leaves the orchard otherwise we won’t be

able to find her; and when you do find her tell her to stay

where she is. Hurry up… good girl!’

— صفحة 122 —

The Young Housemaid ﴿121﴾

The little maid set off once again to follow the Bedouin

woman while our noble master hurried off to the house

where he picked up ten Syrian pounds,

1 a substantial amount

of money in those days. He thought, ‘This amount will

provide food for her and her family for about two months or

more.’ Then he returned to his seat in the orchard where he

sat waiting for the little girl to return.

A long time passed, but the little maid had still not

returned! Mohammad Emin was becoming most concerned

that the poor woman might leave without getting the money

and her family would stay hungry. Time passed as he sat in

the orchard, his concern for the plight of the Bedouin

woman growing by the minute, when eventually he saw the

little girl ambling along in the distance, stopping to look at

flowers or other distractions, chewing gum and blowing

bubbles, seemingly without a care in the world.

He called her to hurry, ‘Where’s the woman?’ he asked,

‘did you stop her?’

‘No,’ she replied in a cold, casual manner, ‘I didn’t.’

When he heard this, he was furious because of her

coolness and indolence, so he cursed her father. ﴿2﴾

When the little girl heard him swearing about her father,

she bowed her head, stopped chewing her gum, and her

1 At that time, one golden lira was equal to five Syrian pounds; so, ten Syrian

pounds came to two golden liras.

2 By cursing the girl’s father the noble scholar meant the devil that was

clinging to her spirit and whispering in her heart that she should delay. So, the

scholar’s swearing shook her which made the devil flee. Truly, every action of

this man was for nothing but good.

— صفحة 123 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿122﴾

lower lip began to tremble. She was heartbroken. As for the

noble master, he called his three sons to come to him at

once; and barely a few minutes had passed before they were

all standing in front of him awaiting his order. He put his

hand into his pocket and brought out two notes, each one

with a value of ten Syrian pounds. He gave one to the eldest

son, Fathi, and one to the other two. He pointed towards

the two roads leading to town and said to them, ‘You, Salah

and Walid, go along this way; and you, Fathi, follow that

one. When you find this Bedouin woman (and here he

described her) give her the ten pounds then come back home

quickly. Have you understood?’

‘Yes father, we’ll do as you ask,’ the three sons replied

and darted off to carry out the task.

No more than fifteen minutes had passed when the

three sons came back one after another, having found the

woman and given her the money. They related to their

father how she had taken the note and begun to touch it as

if she couldn’t believe her eyes… she wanted to be sure that

it was real and not a dream… she had become oblivious to

everything around her. As soon as she was able to believe

her good fortune she rushed off to her family overcome

with relief and happiness.

When Mohammad Emin heard this he was so pleased

and his heart felt at ease. But after a few minutes, he felt the

pains of colic and diarrhea worsening, so he held his stomach

and ran quickly towards the water closet, when suddenly a

— صفحة 124 —

The Young Housemaid ﴿123﴾

low-hanging branch struck his forehead. The impact was

extremely painful, yet the griping pains in his stomach were

rapidly become much more intense, so he ignored the pain

of the blow and hurried towards the water closet as fast as

possible.

But once there, and having found relief from the pains

in his stomach, he began to wonder why he should have

been struck by the branch, saying, ‘Oh my God! What have

I done wrong? I fed the poor woman twice, and what’s

more, I gave her enough money to provide food for her and

her family for at least two months. So, why did the branch

hit me?’

No sooner had he spoken these heartfelt words than he

heard a call coming from within his heart, ‘What about that

poor child? Why did you swear about her father and hurt her

feelings? It’s true that you gave that poor woman enough

food to satisfy her hunger, and it’s also true that you gave her

enough money to provide for her family’s needs for two

months or more. You will be rewarded for this, but what

about that little girl, why did you break her heart?’ He

replied secretly to the question, ‘Yes, I did that for the poor

woman’, yet the voice answered, ‘The favour you have done

for that woman will bring you the reward you are worthy of,

but the act you have done towards the little girl brought you

punishment.’

At that moment all became clear; he understood why the

branch had struck his forehead. He washed his hands, and

— صفحة 125 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿124﴾

without further delay he went towards the little girl who

had not moved, and spoke to her kindly, ‘Are you sad? Are

you upset?’ (it is a characteristic of the Bedouins that they

take to heart any swearword against their father). At this

the little girl bowed her head down showing she was very

sad and deeply affected by his words. Then Mohammad

Emin said to her, ‘Now you can ask me for whatever you

want and I will fulfil all of your wishes.’

As soon as she heard his words she felt happy and joyful.

Smiling again, she raised her head, and quickly listed her

wishes, ‘A dress, a golden bracelet, and a pair of shoes.’

Immediately, Mohammad Emin called his son-in-law

who soon answered him saying, ‘Yes, uncle, what can I do

for you?’

‘I want you to go into Damascus at once to buy the

following items for this girl: a dress, a golden bracelet and a

pair of shoes. Off you go and take her with you.’

Being loath to go just then, the son-in-law answered, ‘But

sir, it’s afternoon now, people usually go for a stroll at this

time of the day… it’s the time to relax and enjoy oneself…

and as the proverb says, “Go shopping in the morning, not

in the evening.” So, tomorrow I will go and buy whatever

she wants.’

‘No! Go right now,’ said Mohammad Emin, who was not

only the younger man’s father-in-law but also his guide and

teacher in religion. When the younger man saw his father-in-

law’s insistence on the matter, he unwillingly responded to

— صفحة 126 —

The Young Housemaid ﴿125﴾

his request and went to Damascus with the little girl where

he bought for her a dress, a golden bracelet and a pair of

shoes.

So, dear reader, take this story to heart and see what an

important lesson one can learn from it! It is a true event that

presents to us a clear example of how Godly Justice manifests

itself in this universe among all of His creatures. It tells us

that Al’lah never accepts oppression of any one of His

creatures. He is displeased when somebody is wronged whilst

favour and charity are being rendered to the poor or needy.

God is in every spot on this earth and if a man wrongs

any single creature, anywhere, all his obeisance and worship

will not prevent him from receiving the punishment he

deserves for this wrongdoing. That is because Al’lah is

Merciful to all His creatures.

So you, too, be merciful to them, and will also receive

His Satisfaction. As for the charity you give dear reader,

Al’lah will repay it to you in full, for there is a reward for

every good deed and a punishment for every bad one. The

maxim says, “Do as you would be done by.”

Whomsoever you may deal with, young or old, powerless

man or weak woman, and whomsoever may be under your

patronage and has less power than you have: beware not to

oppress them or to wrong them, otherwise Al’lah will

certainly empower against you someone who is stronger than

you. So, “Judge not, that you be not judged.”

And praise be to God, at the beginning and at the end.

— صفحة 127 — ﴿126﴾

Do not Steal and It Will Be Given

t was a moonless night, and darkness prevailed. Silence

had spread its wings across the land… and the suspicion

of lurking monsters created a kind of wonder.

The setting for this story is one of the farms in west

Ghutah (al-Hamah) where Mohammad Emin had leased an

apple orchard in which was situated a beautiful rural house

where he would spend the warm summer months.

At midnight, when total silence prevailed, our guide,

Mohammad Emin Sheikho, sat contemplating the events of

the day, thinking them over and planning his programme

and arrangements for the following day as he had always

been accustomed to do… until, eventually, sleep began to

steal over him.

Suddenly, this tranquility was interrupted by the soft

sounds of vague movements like the sound of dry leaves

being rustled by a gentle breeze. It seemed that the sounds

were coming from the farm so he listened attentively and

the sounds became clearer.

He tiptoed into the orchard, where he moved lightly

between the trees and followed the direction of the sound,

— صفحة 128 —

Do not Steal and It Will Be Given ﴿127﴾

and when he drew close to its source, he saw two ghostly

shapes – their features hidden by the darkness – engrossed

in picking the apples and putting them into a big sack that

they held between them.

Giving no sign of his presence, Mohammad Emin

returned to his house moving as lightly as the breeze, and

picked up his pistol, which was always kept under his pillow;

he quickly loaded it, and went back to where he had seen the

thieves. He approached them stealthily and when they were

in range he stopped and aimed his pistol at them with the

customary accuracy and skill for which he was renowned,

and then he fired. The bullet passed between them, and with

the stillness of the night and deadly quiet of the universe the

sound was magnified and they thought it was a cannonball;

they were terrified and rushed off leaving everything behind

them as if they were frightened donkeys fleeing from a fierce

wild animal. They ran hard and fast, striding out so that

their heels almost kicked their backsides. Then Mohammad

Emin fired another bullet which just missed their heads, and

they ran all the faster in their rush to escape.

When they reached the fence, the first one jumped over

to the slope beyond but then lost his balance and slid all the

way down it and, scrambling to his feet, he ran away. And

when the second one jumped, his foot became caught in

the struts of the fence, but his weight propelled him

forwards, and he rolled down the slope unable to believe

that he might escape; unfortunately for him every time his

— صفحة 129 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿128﴾

abdomen bumped on the ground, and because of the fear

that the bullets had provoked in him, he released noxious

body odours, which amused the spirit of Mohammad

Emin, so he laughed out loud. He was delighted that he

had provoked great fear in the hearts of the good-for-

nothings who would steal from him.

Then suddenly… Oh!… How terrible!

A glittering blade appeared above our man’s head… he

thought that there was a third man with them whom he

had failed to notice… so he bent down sharply and briskly

jumped about one and a half metres backwards, and landed

sitting on the ground… and the blade fell in the exact place

he had just been standing: this movement was a tactic he

had adopted when chasing after criminals and punishing

them. And then, in the twinkling of an eye he grabbed his

pistol and pointed it at the person he thought was attacking

him, and at the precise moment that his hand squeezed the

trigger, he saw the long hair of a woman on someone he

thought to be a man; so in less than the blink of an eye he

pointed the muzzle upwards and the bullet missed its mark

with only a split second to spare… then he cried out, ‘Um

Fathi!’

It was, indeed, his own wife; she was thunderstruck when

she heard his voice and her legs buckled beneath her, for the

supposed intruder was none other than her husband!

When she heard the sound of the first shot, she thought

that criminals had already attacked her husband, so she

— صفحة 130 —

Do not Steal and It Will Be Given ﴿129﴾

hurried in the darkness to the farming implements leaning

against the wall beside the orchard gate and grabbed an axe.

She had then rushed towards the sound of the firing and

brought the axe down towards the supposed intruder’s

head, but he eluded the blow with that amazing leap.

What a moment! Whenever anyone thought about it his

spirit trembled, praising God and thanking Him, and his

heart would submit to Him for the extreme Mercy and great

Care which He, the Almighty, deals to those who are truly

obedient to Him. God saved both Mohammad Emin and

his wife at precisely the same moment for His Care had

intervened at exactly the right time… how Great You are my

God – how Great You are! And how Great Your Power is!

After sunrise the following morning, Mohammad Emin

found a huge sack half-filled with apples and another empty

one at the spot where the incident had taken place. The tree

from which the two robbers had been picking apples bore

the finest and largest fruits and were the best in the orchard,

indicating that the thieves had prior knowledge of the place

before attempting to steal the fruit.

The following morning, the local mayor passed by the

orchard of our great scholar and after greeting one another

he said, ‘What’s the matter, Oh Bey? Yesterday we heard

the sound of shooting coming from your house… what

happened?’

Our man looked at him… it was quite clear from the

expression on the mayor’s face that he knew the thieves, for the

chapters.title: صفحة 131 - 140 (Stories of the Scholar)
chapters.html:
— صفحة 131 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿130﴾

village was small and had few inhabitants, so it was obvious

that they knew who might do such deeds… besides, some of

them looked on such actions as a kind of rite of manhood and

they prided themselves on recounting it to those who were of

similar character and frequented the coffeehouses.

God says, “Nor did they forbid one another the

iniquities which they committed: evil indeed were the

deeds which they did.” ﴿1﴾

Our honest man turned to the mayor and said, ‘Yes…

two men tried to steal apples from my orchard but they

managed to escape under cover of darkness, otherwise I

would have ended their wicked lives.’

The mayor was astonished and asked, ‘Would you kill

two men for a few apples?’

Mohammad Emin replied strongly, bravely and firmly,

‘Yes… I’d kill them for stealing even one apple.’

The mayor felt a sense of awe and a strange reverence spread

into his spirit such as one might feel when confronting a lion.

He read indisputable signs of strength and determination in the

character of the courageous man standing before him; thereafter

this is what deterred him and the people of the village from

committing such unlawful acts.

And, in fact, no-one dared even to approach the orchard

after that event.

With this single act Mohammad Emin gave us a practical

lesson on how to weed out an alarming social disease that

1 The Holy Qur’an, Fortress (Surah) 5, The Feast (al-Ma’ida), verse 79.

— صفحة 132 —

Do not Steal and It Will Be Given ﴿131﴾

might otherwise destroy the pillars of the community and

degrade mankind. His mercy extended to the thieves

themselves for he turned them away from the evil enclosed

within their spirits. This, then, is something which reflects

on the entire community, so that safety, peace and cordiality

can prevail over all the land and criminals can turn to

fruitful, honest work if they always find that there is

someone who will stand up to them and deter them.

Some time later, this humane man offered more than

half the fruit of the orchard as gifts to the mayor and people

of the village for them to eat lawfully.

— صفحة 133 — ﴿132﴾

The Magician Is Thwarted in His Plans

n a large room, a number of men sat gathered in a circle,

listening to a soothing and pleasant discourse. Their faces

displayed expressions of great pleasure and enjoyment, so

one might think they appeared to have left behind this world

and all its troubles and strife.

At the front of the room, sat a broad-shouldered man

with a very pale face, but with rosy cheeks that served only

to enhance his beauty. His charming green eyes shone with

allure and liveliness. He appeared to have been encompassed

by a great Godly Solemnity, and displayed signs of

exceptional fortitude crowned with signs of compassion. His

assembly was very open and untroubled and was enhanced

by his imposing speech. He was reciting interpretations of

the Holy Qur’an that were overwhelming the hearts of his

disciples and uplifting them to endless, sublime paradises. At

the end of the lesson, and after performing their prayers to

God, the audience went one by one to address their guide,

then respectfully began to take their leave of him. A few of

them were still there when two of them approached him and

one began to talk as the other nodded in agreement. The

— صفحة 134 —

The Magician Is Thwarted in His Plans ﴿133﴾

two men had recently joined this circle of the great guide.

The man said, ‘Oh, sir! There is a man whose character we

do not know very well at all. We suspect that he is one of

the true men of Al’lah who have supernatural powers,

although he is not Arab.’

He peered at them, saying, ‘Who is he? What do you

mean?’

The new disciple said, ‘Oh, sir! This news is being passed

around by word of mouth. People are talking constantly

about a foreigner that has come to Damascus and established

himself in the main square of al-Marjah. He has opened a

shop there and has started receiving people who ask him

the answer to anything you may wish to ask him about.

‘The odd thing, sir, is that he asks his visitors, whoever

they are, to keep their questions secret, and not tell anyone

what they are. He then takes out a white piece of paper,

which is totally blank, folds it and places it inside a book

lying on the table before the visitor. Then he excuses himself

and goes to his private room for a few minutes. After that he

comes out and retrieving the piece of paper he opens it to

disclose that there is now written the question or wish that is

hidden inside his visitor’s spirit, as well as the reply to the

query. All of that costs one golden lira, sir!’

The eminent guide, Mohammad Emin Sheikho said,

‘What? What are you saying, my son?! He is nothing more

than a human devil who is dealing with evil djinns.’

— صفحة 135 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿134﴾

The speaker replied, backed up by his companion, ‘But

his deeds are really amazing and strange. Sir! Do you know

that, once, a man who had decided to drill a well in the

region he came from, went into this shop. He kept his idea

to himself and spoke of it to no-one. So, when the foreigner

drew out the paper, his answer appeared on it, written in

beautiful Arabic script. It stated, “Drill deeply, and you

shall succeed”.’

The other man added, ‘Yes, sir! We have seen this with

our very own eyes! But what a disappointment the advice

turned out to be! Although the man dug deeply and

burdened himself with huge expenses, eventually the digger

reached bedrock, and not a single drop of water trickled out!’

The first man then added, ‘Another man came to him,

keeping secret his wish to travel to a foreign country to

engage in trade there. He wanted to know whether or not

he would prosper in this course of action. So, when the

foreigner drew out the paper, he found a clear reply written

there that said, “Travel, and you shall prosper!” – and there

are many other men, sir, who have come seeking answers to

their questions. What’s more, if the person who came to

him was not Arab, but of a different nationality, he would

find the paper written in his own language, and that is the

wonder of wonders! By God, this person surely has a

strange, secret gift – doesn’t he, sir?!’

Mohammad Emin laughed and said, ‘Haven’t I already

told you, my sons, that all of his deeds are achieved by means

— صفحة 136 —

The Magician Is Thwarted in His Plans ﴿135﴾

of devils? And he is a human devil. He performs such deeds

with the help of the blind associates of the djinn who help

the likes of him. Haven’t you heard of Al’lah’s Saying in His

Holy Qur’an, “And that there were men of mankind

sought the help of men of djinn, but they added them

nothing other than more strain.” ﴿1﴾

‘Indeed my sons, his actions are those of a magician who

will never prosper whatever he does. There is nothing

unusual about him, because he has withdrawn from Al’lah

and his heart has turned away from Him. He has shunned

his Creator to the extent that he, himself, has willingly

become a devil, adhered to the devils of the djinn. They have

used him to serve their evil purposes of harming creation and

turning the beings of creation away from Al’lah. With such

deeds he aspires only to two things: one of them is money;

the second, that is worse, is to make people turn away from

their love and appreciation of God, so as to make them

glorify him instead. He makes them turn their spirits

towards him, and admire his deeds; but meanwhile he is far

from Al’lah and his spirit is in torment. Through his distance

from God and through people’s directing themselves

towards him – appreciating his deeds and apparent wonders

– he enables devils to creep into them. As a result, these

people are at risk of having spiritual and psychic diseases

inflicted upon them, and so they withdraw from their

Provider and mistrust Him.

1 The Holy Qur’an, Fortress (Surah) 72, The Jinn (al-Jinn), verse 6.

— صفحة 137 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿136﴾

‘That is, they hold serious doubts about Him just like this

sorcerer does. Thus, they forfeit everything, and their spirits

fall into darkness and turn away from Al’lah. This is what he

seeks, which is the same thing that is sought by the failure,

Satan, and is his ultimate purpose. Because of his envy and

the grudges he bears, the loser always tries to bring others

down along with him .

‘Through the story of our master Adam (pth) and the

original Satan, we can glean a warning and a lesson so that we

become well aware of his enmity. Then we can avoid being

deceived by Satan. It shows that the one you are speaking

about is none other than an enchanter who transmits what is

concealed by humanity by means of his own and others’

maleficent djinn associates; that is, by means of the devils.

‘Had man resorted to his Provider and fully sought refuge

in Him, this sorcerer would not have been able to deceive

you into thinking him to be one of Al’lah’s righteous men.

‘So do not be deceived by this trickery, my sons. The sign

of God’s true men is that they draw our attention, our

thoughts and appreciation to our Creator, the One Who is

Gracious and Obliging for all creation: it is He Who

provides food, drink, and life. They direct our spirits towards

Him through thinking of creation and of the Almighty’s

Miracles, such as the sun, the moon, the stars, clouds, rain,

plants and trees, and all of the countless other gifts with

which He supports us. Then they appreciate Him as they

appreciate His Benevolence to them in providing for them,

— صفحة 138 —

The Magician Is Thwarted in His Plans ﴿137﴾

and consequently, they turn to Him with feelings of love.

This is their sign. They never ascribe any action to

themselves at all, nor do they direct people anywhere other

than towards God and His Envoy (cpth). They do not

practise acts which are forbidden and in contravention of

cogent thought and sound logic. These are nothing but

occult matters that turn people away and alienate them from

the right process of thought and sound judgement.’

With his distinguished and rational words, the noble

master continued to gently admonish these two disciples

who had newly attached themselves to him. At the end of his

speech, he turned to the questioner and said, ‘In any case,

tomorrow we shall go to see him together. What do you

think of that, my sons?’

Eager and curious to know the outcome, they both said,

‘An excellent idea! Whatever you say, sir!’

The next day, the two men accompanied the great

master to the supposed “master of wonders and oddities.”

They reached the place where this foreigner had established

himself in a large shop inside which there was a small room.

Mohammad Emin entered first, with his two followers

close behind.

The sorcerer was sitting on a chair near an Arab man,

undoubtedly a translator employed by the former to help

him to perform his acts. The translator rose to his feet and

said, ‘Welcome… come in, please.’ The foreigner glanced at

the venerable master with brief, shifty glances, and then cast

— صفحة 139 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿138﴾

his eyes elsewhere as though the sight of Mohammad Emin

displeased or unnerved him. He turned his attention to his

translator, requesting him to ask his visitors what they

wanted. When he found out that they were going to keep

the subject to themselves as usual, he asked the translator to

tell the master to think of something and share the thought

with no-one.

The virtuous master did so, and then said to the

translator, ‘I have thought of something… I’m ready.’ And

then he placed a golden lira on the table. The enchanter

brought out a white sheet of paper and took care to show

the spectators that it was completely blank. Then, he folded

it in the middle and put it inside a book that was on the

table near them. He quickly entered his small room and

shut the door behind him. As usual, only a few minutes

passed before he came out, but now there was something

rather strange about him! He had gone into the room in a

very sprightly manner, but when he came out he appeared

to be stressed and exhausted, contrary to his usual manner.

He took the folded paper from the book which had

remained in place on the table and when he unfolded it, the

colour of his face took on a greyish tinge. The paper was

still white and blank, which was totally different from the

usual situation after he emerged from his room.

The two questioners looked at the paper and saw that

there was nothing written there, and their surprise was

clearly visible on their faces. They turned their gaze towards

— صفحة 140 —

The Magician Is Thwarted in His Plans ﴿139﴾

the dull-faced man, regarding him with a questioning look,

and not knowing what to think. But when they looked at

their eminent guide, they noticed that a dignified expression

of confidence and tranquility had appeared on his face. He

was standing there as normal, displaying his usual proud

posture.

As for the translator, he was looking about himself

hesitantly, sometimes at the foreigner and sometimes at

Mohammad Emin. The foreigner remained silent for a short

time and continued to look steadily at the blank page,

nervously biting at his lower lip. He seemed to be rather

confused. A few minutes passed… silence prevailed. The only

interaction between them consisted of mutual, questioning

glances which expressed nothing but an enigma, as it

emanated from the language of the spirit. Suddenly, the

foreigner turned and spoke to the translator who, in turn,

addressed Mohammad Emin, saying,

‘You did not think of a secret question!’

Mohammad Emin said with a smile, ‘Tell him that I

did!’

Then, the man returned the sheet of paper to its place, just

as it was, then turned and rapidly went back into his small

room. The great guide turned to his two disciples, talking to

them in a sublime and noble fashion about Al’lah’s Majesty

which fully attract people’s hearts. A quarter of an hour

passed, which made the translator look at his watch in

astonishment, as he had not been accustomed to such delays

chapters.title: صفحة 141 - 150 (Stories of the Scholar)
chapters.html:
— صفحة 141 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿140﴾

from this “master of marvels” in the past. This was the first

time he had stayed in his room for such a long time in order

to disclose a secret. After about twenty minutes, the sorcerer

came out of the room looking sweaty and exhausted. He was

frowning and sullen, as if he had just been weeping over his

bad luck on that unfortunate day. He approached the group

with heavy steps, and stood with his head bowed before our

dignified master, and unfolded the paper. Once again, the

paper was spotless… and blank! The translator and the two

disciples looked at it with an air of amazement, with many

foreigner, the misery on his face appeared to be aggravated

and he became gloomier still. He turned to the imperturbable

master – whose face was still bright, luminous and clear – and

he said to Mohammad Emin through his translator,

‘No! No! You definitely did not think of a secret

The generous master said to the translator, ‘Tell him

that yes, I did.’

The foreigner replied through the translator, ‘If he has

really done so, let him secretly and privately tell you what

he has thought of, out of my earshot. Also tell him that you

will stay close to him and will not come near me.’

When the noble master was told of this request, he smiled

and said, ‘As he likes!’ and then crossed to the translator in

two short steps, and the latter drew close to Mohammad

Emin who whispered to him what he had intended as his

— صفحة 142 —

The Magician Is Thwarted in His Plans ﴿141﴾

secret question, saying, ‘I want him to inform me about

Mohammad ibn Abdullah: communication with Al’lah and

peace are through him.’

During this exchange, the “master of wonders” was

standing away from them, but was minutely scrutinizing them

with his black eyes and closely observing the situation. After

the information had been passed on, he signalled to the

translator, asking if he had been told the secret thought. The

latter indicated that he had. The enchanter then returned to

his room and shut the door. He stayed there even longer than

the previous time, in fact nearly half an hour had passed

before he reappeared. Then, when at last he came out, he

looked almost as though he had been given a severe beating,

to the point that he appeared weak and extremely listless. He

was sweating and staggering around, as if unable to bear the

weight of his own body. When he opened the folded sheet, he

found that it was just the same as it had been. Nothing had

changed… it was still white and blank! He remained silent a

little longer, thinking about the problem of his failure that

day, and then he seemed to realise the cause. He knew that, in

the words of the saying, there were still some “sentinels who

had never been neglectful of foxes”. Truly, he was most

surprised and deeply shocked by this fact. His expectations

had been smashed. He had been thinking that this country no

longer believed in the true faith, and that, therefore, he would

meet no barrier in spreading his corruption. But unfortunately

for him, he had been frustrated in his aim.

— صفحة 143 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿142﴾

The virtuous master turned and said to the translator,

‘Tell him that his devil can never approach our pure and

honourable Prophet, Master Mohammad (cpth). If he had

tried to do that, he would have been burned by his Godly

Light.’ After remaining speechless for a while, the sorcerer

turned to his audience and told his translator to inform

those present that his usual ability and spiritual status were

not functioning that day, but if they were to return the next

day, they would have their questions answered. Here,

Mohammad Emin smiled and said to his two companions,

‘You will not find him here tomorrow, for he will certainly

abscond.’ Then he took back his golden lira and put it in

his pocket. By the following day, the magician had fled

from Syria and gone back to his own country, disappointed

and despondent. He had been planning to resume his tour

throughout all the provinces of the country of Syria, from

Homs to Hama to Aleppo, but had been thwarted in this

dishonest ambition by Mohammad Emin Sheikho.

— صفحة 144 — ﴿143﴾

Almsgiving Can Work Miracles

t’s neither a far-fetched tale, nor a myth! The following

tells of a true incident.

A story told truthfully and honestly, without exaggeration

or imagination, serves as a lesson for all, and has no aim other

than spreading goodwill, love and guidance by Al’lah’s Will.

The Grandeur of God and His great Love for mankind is the

main theme of what we are about to relate.

Al’lah’s Mercy upon His servants entails that He never lets

them indulge and wallow in the mire of their cheap worldly

desires believing that pleasure and comfort are to be found

only in this lowly world and its temporary pleasures. So, the

Almighty brings upon us whatever is necessary to caution us

against the outcome of our own evil deeds which will be as a

raging storm rooting us out from this world whether we wish

it or not, and will then cast us into the abyss. Undoubtedly,

the Almighty showered us with a multitude of gifts when He

created the earth and all that it contains: its seas, mountains

and rivers, the sky and its planets and celestial bodies; and

besides all that, He gave us the ability to hear and see, and the

mind to live and enjoy all this, on one condition: that is that

— صفحة 145 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿144﴾

we should adore no-one and nothing and thus forget the

Creator! Truly, this lowly world was not created simply for

man’s pleasure, but was called into being as a means by which

man should be led to Al’lah.

Then, he who discerns the cause of his own trouble,

which is certainly incumbent upon his deeds, must know

that it is inflicted because of Al’lah’s Mercy, so, he praises,

thanks, and turns to Him in repentance and prays humbly

for relief and the end of his suffering and pain. The

Almighty says, addressing His noble Envoy Mohammad

(cpth), “When My servants ask you about Me, I am

indeed close to them. I respond to the prayer of every

supplicant when he calls on me, but let them first,

willingly, respond to My Call, and believe in Me: that

they may walk in the right way.” ﴿1﴾

As soon as man repents his past sins, God will certainly

comfort him and cure him of whatever ails him: thus He will

open a channel through which he can become acquainted

with Al’lah’s Perfections and Supreme Attributes.

As long as man is sincere and truthful in wanting to be

reinstated on his proper path and then remains loyal to the

pledge he made to Al’lah that he should renounce his

aggression and remain close to his Provider, Al’lah will surely

help him, and turn his affliction into good health and his

distress into well-being. Yet, if our turning back to Him

proves to be of a merely temporary nature, whereby our

1 The Holy Qur’an, Fortress (Surah) 2, The Cow (al-Baqara), verse 186.

— صفحة 146 —

Almsgiving Can Work Miracles ﴿145﴾

personal benefit comes to predominate over our love for

Al’lah and a true desire to return to Him and obey His

Orders, then our affliction shall be like a curse upon us, and

our distress shall be like fire upon our hearts. Should this be

the case, Al’lah would never remove His Temptations from

us and we shall remain lost and confused in darkness until

our time of death, when it would cast us into further and

deeper suffering. God says, “The day that the wrong-doer

gnaws at his own hands, he will say, ‘Oh! I wish that I

had taken a straight path with the Envoy.” ﴿2﴾

This story carries important messages for whoever seeks

redemption: by learning from its lesson, and becoming

enlightened, it gives us the greatest proof of God’s Assertion

of His grand Omnipotence and wise Will when He afflicts

us with relatively slight hardship, disease and torture, in

order to spare us the terrible evil of the greatest torture that

we will suffer if we persist in our infidelity and rejection of

the sources of His Light and Purity.

Saleem Bey was a man of noble Arabic (Hashimi) origin

and was born in Damascus to a wealthy high-bred family. It

was God’s Will that this man should have a brother, our

humane master, Mohammad Emin Sheikho! The two

brothers lived and grew up together in the same home. Their

father died and God determined, according to the wishes of

the elder brother, Saleem, that he would travel to Turkey,

where he settled in the city of Istanbul.

2 The Holy Qur’an, Fortress (Surah) 25, The Criterion (al-Furqan), verse 27.

— صفحة 147 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿146﴾

Eventually, he married the daughter of the then foreign

minister of the Ottoman Empire. Of course, this wife was

suitable for him and his prestigious political and social

position, as he held the rank of general in one of the

Turkish military divisions.

Through his rank and, later, his commercial undertakings,

Saleem Bey was able to amass great wealth thinking that it

would give him security against humiliation and changing

times. As he thought then, and as most people still think

today, money can solve any problem.

As the years passed, Saleem became ever more materialistic

and attached to money and possessions, but as we shall learn,

something unexpected occurred!

He became ill! A debilitating illness crept into his joints

and his limbs began to weaken and lose their ability to move

or to feel. Soon, he became almost paralysed throughout one

side of his body, a condition known as hemiplegia, and this

intensified to such an extent that it seemed as though he

might become bedridden, and, no doubt, human nature

being what it is, he might soon have been forgotten by all

except his close loved ones.

It was then that Saleem knew his health had deteriorated

to a critical level, so he sent for many doctors, but it was in

vain, as they all held a unanimous opinion on the outcome!

‘So, you don’t have any remedy for me! You can’t even

stop this accursed disease from spreading throughout my

body?’

— صفحة 148 —

Almsgiving Can Work Miracles ﴿147﴾

‘Unfortunately, no! We have no medicine for this affliction

and we can only suppose that your days are numbered. You

may have no more than fifteen days and during this time you

may become paralysed and confined to bed. May Al’lah

preserve you and lessen your pain.’

At this moment, the patient sank down to the lowest

depths of sorrow and despair… and lay in his bed with

many thoughts running through his mind,

‘I have spent my life looking for fortune, and when I got

it, it was never truly mine nor did I make good use of it…

and here I am about to depart this world and leave it all

behind! Oh, my brother! Where are you now? Something

in my heart is calling me to you! I must tell you that I’m

ill… I must write to you. I wish I could travel and return to

the land of my forefathers… to my mother, my history…

my childhood… to you, my dear brother in Damascus…

‘I want nothing more from this inferior world for it

offers false promises! And as for money… it should be

incinerated and thrown into the depths of the sea… I don’t

want it if it can’t help me. I have desperate feelings of loss

and homesickness, loneliness, and a yearning for the past…

so many memories following one after the other before my

very eyes… I cannot sleep for my eyes will not close, fearing

death, my unknown fate, and that the darkness of the grave

will suffocate me!

‘Oh my Provider! How can I escape from all that? My

God! I admit my weakness and undeniable need for You,

so, will You please release me?’

— صفحة 149 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿148﴾

His conscience was in turmoil, although those around

him did not notice. And he realised how much he needed to

see his brother and the urgency of writing to him, informing

him of his illness, and asking for his advice respecting his

assets and making arrangements for who should inherit

them. ‘How much should I bequeath to whom? Who should

inherit my personal property?… I know that I’m not long

for this world.’

The telegram carrying the sad news was sent without delay

and when Mohammad Emin read it and learnt of Saleem’s

illness, he was deeply saddened by his brother’s predicament;

he realised too that his brother was showing great repentance

for past deeds and his life which had been spent as though on

a train carrying him from one stop to another in this world,

until he suddenly found himself reaching the final station and

his inevitable departure from the train, leaving behind the

family, the money, and all the memories, to go to an

unknown world in which only those who have been

illuminated by Al’lah’s Light will live happily.

However, our man always hoped for the best outcome,

and he had great confidence in God. He was sure of Al’lah’s

Omnipotence to cure and restore his brother’s health and

grant him a happy and healthy life on condition that he

should understand that the real reason for his present distress

was Al’lah’s Compassion, for He says, “It is possible that

you dislike a thing though it is good for you.”

3 This was a

3 The Holy Qur’an, Fortress (Surah) 2, The Cow (al-Baqara), verse 216.

— صفحة 150 —

Almsgiving Can Work Miracles ﴿149﴾

final great chance to change his ways and habits and spend

his fortune as God decreed and which would cause him to

draw closer to His Presence, and ensure that he would

become enlightened by His Light.

‘There’s no time to waste! Every passing day will be against

the interests of my dear brother. I must reply immediately.’

So, he sent him a telegram calling upon that which is more

important than money, inheritance and bequests, and his

answer contained the following,

‘In the Name of God, the All-Compassionate, the All-

Merciful.

Dear brother Saleem, may Al’lah preserve you.

‘I’ve received your letter, in which I’ve read many things.

I’ve read of your longing for your home and family, your

sorrow and regret, and all of your inner confusion.

‘I know that you are in a bad way but I want you to be

totally confident that Al’lah is Merciful and Fair, and He is

Omnipotent in all matters. Wouldn’t He Who first created

you and provided abundantly for you be able to cure and

rebuild you again? Surely, as it is He Who inflicts all

disease, He alone can lift it. But this will depend on you

and the decision must be yours.

‘I recommend one important thing to you, which will be

your way to escape from this predicament and draw near to

Al’lah! It’s almsgiving, my dear brother, purely and simply!

‘Since that is our great Messenger’s advice for us, it is

good advice for you too. And all who read this account.

chapters.title: صفحة 151 - 160 (Stories of the Scholar)
chapters.html:
— صفحة 151 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿150﴾

‘Our noble Envoy said, “Help your patients to be

cured by almsgiving.”

‘You have to give alms, Saleem! For this will ensure your

retreat from ill health and achievement of happiness both here

and in the hereafter; by Al’lah’s Will, you’ll recover your

health and resume your journey through this life by Al’lah’s

Light and Care, if you really wish to, and all that is up to your

own free will and determination, of course. I call your

attention to an important point, that is: the donation must be

in proportion to the financial resources of the almsgiver. I

know that you have a large, valuable plot of land in the centre

of Istanbul, and I advise you to build a large complex there

consisting of a basement, stores and offices, and above these

there should be flats, in three sizes and designed as follows:

One bedroom, living room, and facilities, to suit a man

who is debilitated, for instance.

Two bedrooms, living room and facilities for a medium

sized family.

Three bedrooms, living room, and facilities for a big

family.

You should then rent out the basement, the stores and all

the offices except one: this you retain and employ a manager

to control the entire property from there, and give him the

responsibility for calculating the revenues of the project. This

income should then be distributed on a regular basis amongst

those whom you house in these flats, and to other poor

families, orphans and needy, helpless people according to each

one’s needs, so they have the means to live at a basic level.’

— صفحة 152 —

Almsgiving Can Work Miracles ﴿151﴾

He ended his telegram full of hope and prayer to God that

it may be well received by Saleem, and that he might reply

positively, and apply this advice promptly, after establishing a

true and meaningful undertaking between himself and his

Provider.

Saleem’s condition worsened and his sorrowful sighs

increased, tearing into the depths of his heart and bringing

him nothing but further sadness, pain, and hopelessness.

But when our man’s telegram arrived it caused a flash of

hope to light up inside him, which he had not dreamed of.

He perceived a gleam of hope rising from it, so he clung

to it. And yet he lingered a little, wondering, ‘Alms? I’ve

never heard of a thing called “Alms” that can cure an

incurable disease like mine! I don’t care about the land, I no

longer aspire to money or possessions, but if medicine has

been unable to cure or help me, how will almsgiving restore

my health? Oh, my Provider! Is this true?’

While he was in that state of pondering and contemplation,

he dozed and dreamed that his brother came and greeted him.

Mohammad Emin sat beside him talking to him and showing

him great sympathy; he interrupted his loneliness and answered

the questions that came to his mind. He explained to him the

wisdom concealed within almsgiving and the Greatness of

God, and His Potency and Mercy, as he clarified to him the

reason for all disease, and the only remedy for every disease

whatever it may be.

‘Yes, dear brother, it is almsgiving and nothing else. It is

the only way that can bring you closer to God. By giving alms

— صفحة 153 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿152﴾

the spirit becomes sure that Al’lah is pleased with it due to the

good deed it has rendered; therefore it does not hesitate to

draw near to Him, and by its nearness and ascension towards

its Creator, it becomes cured of all ailments and imperfections

which have attached themselves to it in this world; and when

the spirit regains its health, its cure will be reflected in the

body which is like a mirror that reflects the state of the human

spirit.

‘Dear Saleem! Al’lah is Near and He is always ready to

answer your request, but we should be believers and observe

His Orders when asking Him for favours; remain close to

Him and be grateful for His Benefits for He is Al’lah, the

Peerless, the Owner of all perfection Who hears all and

answers all. He is the Truth and the best Disposer of affairs. If

we surrender to Him and put our trust in Him, He will

arrange all that we need, for He owns and controls everything.

So, turn to Him wholeheartedly, dear brother! Pray to Him

and ask Him for whatever you want, then place in His Hands

any offering that you like, so that He may bring you near to

Him and overwhelm you: begin with when you were a single

drop of semen that was formed in a man’s body by a mixture

of many different kinds of food and fruit, and then turned

into an embryo inside your mother’s belly. Ask yourself, who

put you in her belly? Who created you and then provided

everything for you until you became such a wonderful

creation? Who guided you to her breasts which contained

delicious, nutritious milk in quantities that were appropriate

— صفحة 154 —

Almsgiving Can Work Miracles ﴿153﴾

to your age? Contemplate the phases you have passed

through: how you turned from a child to a youth and then to

a grown man! Think of all of that: think of the sun and the

moon, the heaven, the day and the night! Who created all of

that?

‘It is Him, my brother! It is Al’lah.’

At that point, Saleem awoke as though from a long dream

with tears flowing from his eyes. And as came to his senses

after experiencing this vision and reading the words of his

brother, he pondered upon both of them. He sensed the

truth of his words, and believed what he said. He was

overjoyed to see his brother and to hear such wise words

from him. He felt as if something new had been created

inside his spirit; and indeed it had: it was a great love for

Al’lah and His Prophet which he had never known before.

Without further delay, he called his two sons, ‘Come on,

my sons! I want you to send for the civil engineers and the

contractors; we need those who are experts in complex

buildings… I must recover; I must start out as I mean to carry

on! I do not want to die in such a state.’

He was truly enthusiastic and sincere, and far be it from

God to close the doors of His Mercy before anyone that

prays to Him in distress, since he sacrifices what he likes for

His Sake. The noble saying denotes, “No man may become

a believer unless he sacrifices something that he likes.”

Indeed, he carried out his brother’s recommendation to the

letter. He fully understood the juncture he had just passed

— صفحة 155 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿154﴾

through in his life, and the gravity of the coming stage which

would require faithfulness, firm decisions and persistence. He

knew he had to be resolute in his commitment to the

construction of a considerable building on his valuable land to

provide homes and income for needy and helpless people. He

would offer this as a deed dedicated to God, alone, so that he

might become cured of his physical and spiritual diseases

which came as a result of his love for this lowly world and

which had worsened because of his remoteness from God.

Having fulfilled his brother’s advice, he began to monitor

himself and await the results; but in this he was not alone for

Mohammad Emin was with his brother wholeheartedly,

anxious, and about to lose his patience.

‘Oh my God!’ General Saleem soliloquized, ‘Could this

truly happen? Will God actually cure me of this affliction

which His Wisdom inflicted upon me? I really feel better; I

feel that there is something flowing in my veins: something

that has touched my senses and is inspiring me to stand, to

walk and to return; but to where?

‘Shall I return to the same old way of life that I followed?

Shall I return to the primrose path, the life of ease and

pleasure, that I was following and that might end in calamity?

Shall I return to my negligent ways? To my oppression and

ungratefulness? Shall I forget Al’lah once again? Shall I deny

His Favour and Charity? May I return once again to my

disregard and indifference? What good will my health and

wellbeing bring me then?

— صفحة 156 —

Almsgiving Can Work Miracles ﴿155﴾

‘No! By God I do not want to regain my health… not at

all! I do not even wish for it if it enables me to go back to

my old way: a cold and dark path on which every step

would drive me further towards that terrible abode which I

will have chosen by my own free will, and by my work and

shunning; only then will I witness the truth, and the self-

reproach will begin, “Oh my God! How did I come to be

here? Was I deaf? Was I blind to let my feet carry me here?”

At that time, I would find no shelter except a flaming fire

which will be a treatment for my spirit to be cured from its

defects and low diseases!

‘No! No!… And no again! Oh my God! I ask for Your

Pardon! Please God, forgive me! Oh God, please, I’m a

servant standing at Your Doors, wishing to obtain Your

Mercy and Love. Oh God! My spirit has become filled with

love for this world, so please, would You cleanse it by Your

pure Water and Light?

‘Oh my Provider! I beg You to answer my call and not

reject me. Oh my Lord! I promise that I will perform the

communication with You through Your Prophet as long as

I live, and I shall ensure that my wife puts on a veil.’

Indeed, it was not long before he felt himself growing

gradually better, and with this he became more truthful and

persisted in his truthfulness. He invoked God for many

long nights; he cried and asked for His Forgiveness, as he

offered up what he liked to become nearer to God so that

He might accept him and forgive him.

— صفحة 157 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿156﴾

And so he would pass the spiritual test; he could seize his

final opportunity before the doors of his life were shut,

when leaves would fall to the ground as the soul will have

gone up to heaven and the body will have decomposed

under the ground. At that moment, unless he repented, the

spirit would be wandering and full of regret; it would have

no place to settle, neither on earth nor in the sky.

It would live forever in the depths of darkness, loneliness

and fear. There, its laments would ring out, breaking the

silence, shaking the pillars and waking the dead who will

say, ‘Oh our Lord! Send us back so that we may perform

the communication with You and prostrate ourselves to

You.’ But how far! How far it would be! For by then, our

years will have been spent and death will have overtaken us.

As for Saleem, he considered all that he wanted to save

himself from, the woes and evils of that day, so he prepared

himself and cast off all the shackles from his spirit. So, his life-

blood began to flow, his nerves were revived, bones regained

their strength, and his heart beat with joy… and finally, the

smile on his face expressed his overwhelming happiness. There

were, too, fervent expressions of pleasure; and the bright rays

of the sun heralded a new morning, while beautiful spring

flowers bloomed after a long winter, adding to the feeling of

joy. Indeed, the Grand God overwhelmed Saleem with His

Compassion, Tenderness and great Care as He bestowed

pleasure and bliss upon him and planted the seeds of virtue

and goodness in his spirit, in addition to a great desire to

— صفحة 158 —

Almsgiving Can Work Miracles ﴿157﴾

escape a regrettable end. All combined to reflect on his body

which soon recovered and became full of life. His happiness

was complete when he was able to go on foot to the land on

which the charitable project would be constructed; here he

laid the foundation stone for the building which would give

shelter to tens of needy and helpless people and ensure an easy

life for them so that they might forget the times of hunger and

need.

He regained his health and went on to live his new life as

the Almighty wanted him to live. But of course, he would

not forget his brother’s favour and the important role he had

played in his recovery from diseases that had inflicted his

spirit even before his body. He would not stop performing

the communication with God, and, too, he would ask his

modern wife to veil her face and wear religious clothes;

happy that her husband had been restored to good health she

complied willingly.

As for our man, Mohammad Emin, the great happiness

he felt could not be matched either on earth or in heaven,

especially when he saw a picture of his brother which was

enclosed with a letter sent by Saleem where he wrote about

what had happened to him: the trials and tribulations he had

passed through, until he was ultimately restored to health.

Saleem explained that, ‘The commemorative picture was

taken while I was laying the foundation stone by myself’… and

it is still kept in the house of Mohammad Emin, (May God

grant him more sublimation and nearness to His Honour).

— صفحة 159 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿158﴾

In fact, Saleem rendered an exceptional deed when he

sacrificed something that was dear to him to prove his

truthfulness in wishing to gain God’s Satisfaction and

Forgiveness, and to regain his physical and spiritual health,

although he was quite sure that Al’lah has no need of us. On

the contrary, we are in need of Him, for as it states in the

Holy Qur’an, the Almighty says, “Whatever of good you

give benefits your own spirits.” ﴿4﴾

The giving of alms is not to give money for Al’lah to add

to His Treasures, but it is an expression of our truthfulness

and our faith so that if we then follow the straight path

with no deviation we will certainly believe that there is no

god except Al’lah, for this statement means that there is no

doer and no steerer except Al’lah and He is the sole Owner

of power and Possessor of all. So, if you are honest and

truthful in your intention and your direction towards God,

He will fulfill your call and improve your situation.

After recovering from that affliction, Saleem Bey lived

for more than fifteen years.

He watched over the construction of the large building and

over the allocation of the homes it contained among the poor

people and securing their financial assistance. During those

years, he was very active, enjoyed excellent good health, and

lived a far happier life than he had ever lived before.

4 The Holy Qur’an, Fortress (Surah) 2, The Cow (al-Baqara), verse 272.

— صفحة 160 — ﴿159﴾

A Miraculous Feat of Strength

he Almighty God says in the Holy Qur’an, “They

give preference to others, even though they are

in need themselves.” ﴿1﴾

The heat of the midday sun had gradually lessened during

the afternoon; it was now early evening and a welcome breeze

had sprung up. The great master – who was about sixty years

old at the time – was still in his room on the upper floor of

the house where he had spent a relaxing, contemplative

afternoon. His room adjoined a corridor which led to the

main door of his Arab-style house. Um Fathi, his wife, had

begun to clean the passage when suddenly she heard a knock

at the door.

She called out to her husband, ‘Abu Fathi, there’s

someone knocking at the door!’

The august master stood up and went to open the main

door, while his wife remained standing nearby behind the

door of the guest room. He stood at the door looking at the

visitor, and realised it was someone he had ever seen before.

The man standing there before him addressed Mohammad

1 The Holy Qur’an, Fortress (Surah) 59, Creation-Gathering (al-Hashr), verse 9.

chapters.title: صفحة 161 - 170 (Stories of the Scholar)
chapters.html:
— صفحة 161 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿160﴾

Emin hesitantly, as though certain matters weighed heavily

on his mind… but it was his impoverished condition and

obvious dire need which had compelled him to ask for

help. As the wise master looked at the man God revealed to

him, within an instant, the true extent of his need and

suffering: the profound misery and despondency which

arise from poverty and lack of income was displayed clearly

on the stranger’s face.

The Almighty says, “You will recognise them by the

obvious signs: they do not trouble people by begging

from them.” ﴿2﴾

Those people deserve to receive all possible assistance.

The light of this master’s heart and his nearness to Al’lah

granted him the vision to be fully aware of the reality, so we

are given a warning from the Tradition of the Prophet, “Be

cautious of the believer’s insight, as he sees by God’s

Light.”

Mohammad Emin hurried to help the man in his time of

need and raise him out of his state of deprivation and

penury, but there was no help to be found in his pocket as

there were only a few coins: this amount could never satisfy

Mohammad Emin’s customary levels of kindness and

generosity. Furthermore, it would do little to alter the

obvious desperate condition of the pauper standing before

him, or even allay his hunger temporarily. An idea came to

him, so he emptied his pocket of every last coin and gave the

2 The Holy Qur’an, Fortress (Surah) 2, the Cow (al-Baqara), verse 273.

— صفحة 162 —

A Miraculous Feat of Strength ﴿161﴾

money to the wretched man standing before him, saying in a

gentle voice laced with extreme mercy and kindness, ‘Please

take this money and go to bring a pack animal here to my

house, while I bring a sack of wheat to help feed your family

to prevent them from starving to death.’

The desperate man accepted the money gladly: the

master’s gentle words were like water to a thirsty, wilted

plant and he seemed rejuvenated as he grabbed the coins and

rushed away from the house. His helplessness and weakness

had suddenly turned into strength and vigour and he hurried

away to return with a donkey to carry the promised sack of

wheat.

In as much as Mohammad Emin’s words were soothing

and comforting to the heart of that wretched man they came

as a hard shock to his wife! She could hear her husband’s

words as she was close by tending to the garden and watering

the plants and flowers.

She could not believe her ears! She stood dumbfounded,

unable to concentrate on the task at hand, and even stopped

breathing for a few moments, as she remembered what effort

had gone into cleaning the wheat. It had taken her three

whole days of exhausting, back-breaking toil to clean that

sack of wheat which weighed nearly 120 kilograms. For not

only did it need cleaning but it then had to be spread out to

dry in the courtyard, and afterwards she had put it with her

own hands into this large sack to be ready for grinding. And

now, with a mere knock at the door, it would be given away

and all her hard work would have been in vain.

— صفحة 163 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿162﴾

‘Oh, please,’ she thought, ‘let him take whatever he wants

but not this sack of wheat… No! I have worked so hard…

I’ve given my heart and soul to the task of preparing it… I’ve

sweated like a labourer for three whole days.’ A few moments

passed as she pondered this predicament, then she snapped

out of her reverie and thought about what should happen

now

With great determination, she rushed down to the

ground floor where the sack of wheat was lying in the store

room. A few moments later, Mohammad Emin entered the

room heading for the sack of wheat. When she saw him her

suspicions were confirmed and she was overcome with fury

which had settled deep in her heart, and expressed itself in

her strong reaction to his decision which had affected her so

strongly. She was determined to stand her ground beside

the sack of wheat and face up to her husband displaying her

tough, steely will. Then, she said in a tone of voice that

registered her strong disapproval of his actions, ‘Abu Fathi

take anything you want for him except that sack of wheat!!

Upon my blood… upon my soul…’ She was so upset that

it seemed she would not allow this sack to leave the house

even if she sacrificed her life for it. Yet when the humane,

merciful and generous master saw her determination and

objection to his carrying out this good deed, his innate

sense of goodness became aroused to the point that he was

even more determined to carry out his good deed; he cared

for nothing around him, and would not be thwarted by any

emotion however intense it might be.

— صفحة 164 —

A Miraculous Feat of Strength ﴿163﴾

He was more determined than ever to carry out the

humane deed of releasing that miserable man from his poverty

and deprivation which would ensure God’s Satisfaction with

him, Mohammad Emin. So, he lost no more time and dashed

off immediately to put his thoughts into action.

But how was he going to pick up this heavy weight? He

bent over the sack, put both arms around it, and undeterred

by the enormous weight he stood up with new found

strength, denoting the compassion, generosity, zeal, and love

for rendering good and magnificent deeds, that were enfolded

within his spirit.

He drew up to his full height hugging the large, weighty

sack close to his chest. But what was this? It is virtually

impossible for any man, however strong he might be, to

carry such a load in this way: normally it would have to be

carried on a man’s back.

Incredible! This man was almost sixty years old and he

was hoisting a 120 kilogram sack of wheat, a feat that even

the strongest champions would find difficult to achieve.

What kind of steady will and extreme resolution prevailed

over this man’s superhuman physical state, giving it the

strength to carry out this heroic performance? The picture

was quite remarkable, but true!

That amazing sight had really startled and overwhelmed

his wife so her determination was swallowed up in an instant,

as a drop of water is consumed by the sea, thus weakening her

intention and scattering her determination in every direction.

— صفحة 165 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿164﴾

She knew for certain that there was no way to deter her

husband: the deed would be done even if it cost her blood…

soul… life… for how could she stand firm before the

unleashed forces of a stormy sea?

Mohammad Emin was rushing forwards carrying a sack

which weighed 120 kilograms, and if she tried to stop him

she would surely be knocked down and crushed to death

under the combined weight of the sack of flour and her

husband. So, she retreated slowly and stood with her back

against the wall… amazed, astounded, and silent… she

realised that her outburst had served no purpose, so she

calmed down. Still hugging the weighty sack, Mohammad

Emin went up the first three steps, then walked a few paces

on the landing before climbing ten more steps till he

reached the open door of the house.

He staggered out to the road where he put the sack down

in front of the door, as the beggar appeared approaching the

house, followed by a drover leading his donkey; when he

arrived they both lifted the sack on to the back of the animal,

making sure that it was properly balanced. The pauper then

departed after offering heartfelt words of thanks and saying

goodbye to the kindest, most open-handed man he had ever

met during his life. The generous, pure master returned to

his room feeling extremely happy after carrying out that

heroic performance in applying Al’lah’s Command, and not

giving way to the discontent that had been expressed by his

wife. Al’lah’s Satisfaction and the importance of charity had

been uppermost in his mind. He was amazed that he had

— صفحة 166 —

A Miraculous Feat of Strength ﴿165﴾

been able to lift up the immensely heavy sack with relative

ease and climb thirteen steps carrying such a weight!!

Some time after this incident, when money became

available, Mohammad Emin bought another sack of wheat

to replace the one that had been given away, and fortunately

for Um Fathi this wheat had already been cleaned and dried.

Mohammad Emin went to lift it as he had lifted the previous

sack but failed to lift it off the floor… in fact he could not

move it at all!

With what kind of love for good, and zeal for attaining

God’s Satisfaction, had his pure and honest spirit been

endowed to enable him to achieve that incredible feat?

Truly this super power is the fruit of the truthfulness

and desire of Mohammad Emin’s spirit to achieve the

Approval of Al’lah the Great, Who says, “The righteous

will surely drink from a cup mixed with overwhelming

delight. A spring from which Al’lah’s servants will drink

their fill, causing it to gush forth abundantly. They fulfil

the vow; and they fear a Day of widespread woes. They

willingly give food, for the love of Him, to the poor, the

orphan, and the captive,” and when they do this they say

to themselves, “We feed you only for the Sake of God; we

seek neither recompense nor thanks from you.” ﴿3﴾

Truly, that faithful man enriched the earth with deeds of

glory and sublimity, the veracity of which has been proved

by his miraculous performances.

In his presence blessings always prevailed!

3 The Holy Qur’an, Fortress (Surah) 76, Humane Man (al-Insan), verses 5-9.

— صفحة 167 — ﴿166﴾

The Wisdom behind the Marriage Contract

venerable manner with a proud, defensive posture

of pride which he displayed in defence of Al’lah’s

Law and Wisdom: such were his disposition and

principles which demonstrated his great zeal and support for

his belief and which he employed to fend off the accusations

aimed at contesting God’s predominant Religion.

The true guide, Mohammad Emin Sheikho, was born in

the al-Ward section in the Sarouja quarter in Damascus. He

lived there until he was eighteen years old when he moved to

another section in al-Muhajireen quarter which stands on the

slope of Mount Qasiyun in Damascus. When he left the al-

Ward section he left behind the imprint of so many

wonderful memories and a great number of friends and

loved ones. Days, months and years followed in quick

succession until forty years had passed during which he

assumed the mission of guidance as his heart’s eye was

opened and his spirit was illuminated by God’s Light, so that

he became an eternal eminent scholar whom Al’lah endowed

with great knowledge and wisdom. Therefore, a great circle

of people assembled around him and he invited them to

— صفحة 168 —

The Wisdom behind the Marriage Contract ﴿167﴾

Al’lah with certainty, showing them the way of believing in

God and how to communicate with Him, the Almighty.

As already mentioned, when he left Sarouja quarter (al-

Ward section), he left behind many dear friends, amongst

whom was Abu al-Yeser Abdeen. In the old neighborhood a

strong, long-lasting friendship had developed between

them. This friend was one of the important men of religion

and a medical professor in his time. He was appointed to

the post of General Mufti of Syria, apart from holding the

post of medical professor.

Student physicians could not graduate unless they passed

the final examination which he, himself, set for them. It is an

extremely exacting exam, unlike any other. He asked the

professor did not allow him to pass the exam as the souls of

people are entrusted to their hands. Therefore, the aspiring

physicians should be astute in medical matters and worthy of

assuming this serious position and great responsibility.

So, as we see, this man carried the burden of the two

weighty tasks simultaneously: he read a lot of religious books

and was extremely interested in this field. As a young man, he

regularly attended the sessions of sheikhs (religious scholars)

and followed their lessons; when he grew up he, too, became a

sheikh and studied the religion assiduously until eventually he

assumed the post of General Mufti of Syria.

One day, our venerable scholar went to his old house, and

whilst there he was happy to visit his old friend, Abu al-Yeser

— صفحة 169 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿168﴾

Abdeen. When he entered the professor’s house he found

some medical students questioning him about religious

matters, ‘Professor… Islam made marriage conditional upon

a certain regulation and without this contract no marriage

can be finalised and consummated: in fact, Islam considers

such marriage as fornication, so what is the actual function

of this contract? And what purpose does this written

marriage contract serve in Islam? If the man and woman love

and desire one other and each of them wants the other to be

his or her partner, why do they need a written contract? And

is it of such importance that marriage is considered adultery

without it? It is nothing more than a piece of paper… and

how can a piece of paper have any bearing on the subject?’

Professor Abu al-Yesser was astonished at these strange

allowed… it’s forbidden… it’s apostasy… what are you

saying? Of course it’s necessary, my sons… yes… yes… this

document is necessary, otherwise it will be adultery and not

a legalised marriage.’

When they heard his reply they persisted with their

evidence. They repeated, ‘But if they truly love one another…

what purpose will the document serve? We think that Islam is

upholding a useless regulation.’

The good sheikh became even more upset and zealous in

defence of his religion, and he cried loudly, ‘No… no… I

don’t want to hear any more talk of disbelief and banned

— صفحة 170 —

The Wisdom behind the Marriage Contract ﴿169﴾

topics… without this contract marriage is prohibited… the

devil has taken control of you today and cloaked you in the

garment of disbelief… he’s imposed his own wrongful ideas

upon you… I ask Al’lah’s Forgiveness… I ask Al’lah’s

Forgiveness… there is no might or power except by God.’

But, unfortunately, his outburst served only to increase

the students’ laughter and jibes, and they repeated their

means nothing and serves no purpose!’ Then they burst out

laughing, as they directed their looks and words of mockery

at the professor… ‘Tell us: should it be a special type of

paper? Or is there a secret contained within it?’

The hapless but honourable sheikh became more and

more angry and no longer knew what to do but heap abuse

upon them in a vain attempt to stop the farce.

In their view, they saw that there was no wisdom nor any

use in that Godly Legislation; the head of all the sheikhs

stood before them but even he was unable to answer them,

so, receiving no conclusive reply, they persisted in repeating

their question in the hearing of the good sheikh, using

sarcastic words, and mocking Islam and its laws because they

considered it out of line with this advanced age. They

insisted that there is no wisdom behind its laws, nor any

benefits folded within its legislation… it is nothing more

than a set of worthless principles and of no relevance in this

mighty civilisation and the worldly sciences which depend

on logic and proof.

chapters.title: صفحة 171 - 177 (Stories of the Scholar)
chapters.html:
— صفحة 171 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿170﴾

Those thoughts settled in their minds and prevented

their hearts from discerning the truth, especially when they

found no-one to stand up to them and refute their thoughts

with logic, and cogent evidence.

Therefore, they accused Islam of futility and ineffectiveness.

If they really wanted to know the truth, they would have asked

their question politely and would not be uncouth and

disrespectful to the good sheikh when they knew that he had

no compelling explanation. But they were determined to accuse

Islam of inadequacy and shortcomings, and that it promoted

superstitions and fanaticism with its useless precepts.

But Al’lah refused to let them continue to stray in their

darkness and wrong themselves, so He directed the venerable

scholar Mohammad Emin Sheikho to go to them.

He went to the home of his old friend and neighbour to

greet him, and there he found him broken-hearted because

of the shocking way the young men had spoken to him.

They had questioned him in a derogatory manner, aiming to

enrage him, but the good man answered within the limits of

his knowledge which failed to satisfy them or stop their

mockery. Mohammad Emin saw what was happening and

heard the on-going talk: as always, his heart was inflamed

with his zeal and love for Islam, and being outraged at

finding his friend in such a state, he went to his defence. He

said to him, ‘Excuse me! Would you please let me answer

their question?’

‘Of course… willingly!’ replied the good sheikh.

— صفحة 172 —

The Wisdom behind the Marriage Contract ﴿171﴾

The group of young physicians turned towards him, and

when they saw his air of gravity and peerless awe, a strange

feeling crept into their spirits, stopping their laughter and

mockery in their tracks, and they turned to listen to him

attentively.

The eminent guide seemed genuinely interested in speaking

to them: there was great truthfulness glowing in his eyes revealed

by his great passion for Islam and Al’lah. This supreme affection

and delicate sensitivity were accompanied by boundless mercy

for that misguided group of young men who were in great need

of guidance to help them out of the depths to which they had

sunk. Mohammad Emin’s reasoning was that if they saw the

sublime facts of the Islamic religion they might turn to it, abide

by its laws, and be saved from unsparing punishment.

The virtuous guide said, ‘Let us suppose that the young

man became fond of the beautiful young woman and they

fell in love… let us then suppose that we refused this

document and they practised love without it, and had

children. Then, what would happen if the infatuated man

died suddenly? Who would support his sons and daughters

and that sad broken-hearted woman after her lover had

departed this life having deflowered her and abandoned her

without insurance, leaving her poverty-stricken, humiliated

and debased? What about the fate of the fatherless children?

Undoubtedly, the inheritors and the family of the departed

young man would come and cast them out to be ruined

since they are illegitimate and their father had passed away,

— صفحة 173 —

Stories of the Scholar ﴿172﴾

leaving his “widow” and progeny to the evils of fending for

themselves.

‘Of course, the heirs – for example, his brother, sister,

father, mother and other relatives – would come to seize,

legitimately, everything the young family had in the way of

furniture, belongings, food, drink and residence, saying to

them, “The inheritance should be for the rightful family

and you will get nothing!”

‘So my brothers, now do you understand the purpose of

the contract of marriage, which you describe as “merely a

piece of paper”, for it makes a virtuous wife from a dissolute

woman, and respectable, legitimate sons instead of criminals

who would show enmity towards the cruel society. So, could

anyone swindle them out of their father’s bequest or render

them homeless to live in poverty? Moreover, due to this

paper, would his partner-in-life be considered as an

uninhibited adulteress or an honourable wife? In the

unmarried state, who would accept her with her sons and

daughters to be a heavy burden and shameful mark of

disgrace? Where is her inheritance? And how would she spend

the rest of her life? Would it be in prostitution after her youth

had wilted? What a hard and bitter life she would face! Yet

who, in fact, would have been responsible for such a situation?

‘That said, let us return to this paper you have ridiculed.

You are wrong! This is the Law of the Merciful God!’

The scholar resumed, ‘So, wouldn’t we, ourselves, have

destroyed the first link of society, which is the family, and

— صفحة 174 —

The Wisdom behind the Marriage Contract ﴿173﴾

consequently destroyed society in its entirety had we

followed this deficient point of view that “they loved one

another”? Now, don’t you see that this contract will provide

lasting evidence to ensure the rights of the wife and the

children and make sure of a secure life for them? What do

you think? Should we still dispense with it?’

Faced with this superior logic and intelligent rebuttal, and

Godly Aid for our enlightened guide, they bowed to the

great wisdom behind Al’lah’s Law and Order, admitting and

confessing the truth and necessity of this legislation, they

said, ‘In fact, we thought the religion to be just madness, but

the reality seems to be different.’

The scholar, Mohammad Emin, went on showing them

that Islam is a religion based on facts and valuable principles,

and its precepts are not at all futile, for it contains nothing

but truth, and that each Godly Command and heavenly

legislation includes deep wisdom and leads to happiness here

and in the Hereafter for one and all. Indeed, the Almighty

wants nothing but happiness and no misery for His creatures

in this world and in the Afterlife, and that is why He sent

His Envoy (cpth) for all people, thus revealing the sublimity

of His Sharia and the grandeur of His Guidance and the

deep wisdom enfolded within every one of His Orders, and

the goodness gained by applying them.

One of the Envoy’s (cpth) instructions about marriage that

has been handed down, without interruption, throughout

Islam, is that the male relatives, friends and neighbours of

the marriage on the day it took place; they should be offered a

banquet of fine foods, including the most delicious sorts of
